sentences.zh: 永安王孝基 淮安王神通 子道彥 孝察 孝同 孝慈 孝友 孝節孝義孝逸

translations.literal: Prince Yong'an Xiaoji; Prince Huai'an Shentong; sons Daoyan, Xiaocha, Xiaotong, Xiaoci, Xiaoyou, Xiaojie, Xiaoyi, and Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong'an Xiaoji; Prince Huai'an Shentong; and his sons Daoyan, Xiaocha, Xiaotong, Xiaoci, Xiaoyou, Xiaojie, Xiaoyi, and Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 襄邑王神符 子德懋 文暕

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu; sons Demao and Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu; his sons Demao and Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 長平王叔良 子孝協 孝斌孝斌子思訓思誨 叔良 弟德良 幼良

translations.literal: Prince of Changping Shuliang; son Xiaoxie; Xiaobin—Xiaobin's sons Sixun and Sihui; Shuliang's younger brothers Deliang and Youliang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changping Shuliang; his son Xiaoxie; Xiaobin—whose sons were Sixun and Sihui; and Shuliang's younger brothers Deliang and Youliang.

sentences.zh: 襄武王琛 河間王孝恭 子晦 孝恭弟 瑊 瑰廬江王瑗 王君廓附

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangwu Chen; Prince of Hejian Xiaogong; son Hui; Xiaogong's younger brothers Jian and Gui; Prince of Lujiang Yuan; Wang Jun'guo appended.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangwu Chen; Prince of Hejian Xiaogong; his son Hui; Xiaogong's younger brothers Jian and Gui; Prince of Lujiang Yuan; with Wang Jun'guo appended.

sentences.zh: 淮陽王道玄 江夏王道宗 隴西王博乂

translations.literal: Prince of Huaiyang Daoxuan; Prince of Jiangxia Daozong; Prince of Longxi Boyi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huaiyang Daoxuan; Prince of Jiangxia Daozong; and Prince of Longxi Boyi.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通，高祖從父弟也。

translations.literal: Prince Huai'an Shentong was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai'an Shentong was a cousin of Emperor Gaozu on his father's side.

sentences.zh: 父亮，隋海州刺史，武德初追封鄭王。

translations.literal: His father Liang had been prefect of Haizhou under the Sui; at the beginning of Wude he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liang had served as prefect of Haizhou under the Sui; at the start of the Wude era he was posthumously created Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 神通，隋末在京師。

translations.literal: Shentong was in the capital at the end of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Sui, Shentong was in the capital.

sentences.zh: 義師起，隋人捕之，神通潛入鄠縣山南，與京師大俠史萬寶、河東裴勣、柳崇禮等舉兵以應義師。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, the Sui sought to arrest him; Shentong secretly entered the mountains south of Hu County, and with the capital champion Shi Wanbao, Hedong's Pei Ji, Liu Chongli, and others raised troops in response to the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began, the Sui authorities tried to seize him; Shentong slipped into the hills south of Hu County and, together with the capital bravo Shi Wanbao, Pei Ji of Hedong, Liu Chongli, and others, raised forces to join the cause.

sentences.zh: 遣使與司竹賊帥何潘仁連結。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to join forces with the Sizhu bandit chief He Panren.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys to ally with He Panren, the bandit leader at Sizhu.

sentences.zh: 潘仁奉平陽公主而至，神通與之合勢，進下鄠縣，眾逾一萬。

translations.literal: Panren came leading Princess Pingyang; Shentong combined forces with him, advanced and took Hu County, and his followers exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Panren arrived at the head of Princess Pingyang's forces; Shentong joined with him, marched down on Hu County, and mustered more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 自稱關中道行軍總管，以史萬寶為副，裴勣為長史，柳崇禮為司馬，令狐德棻為記室。

translations.literal: He styled himself Grand Commander of the Guanzhong Expeditionary Force, appointing Shi Wanbao as deputy, Pei Ji as chief clerk, Liu Chongli as marshal, and Linghu Defen as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed himself Grand Commander of the Guanzhong Expeditionary Force, with Shi Wanbao as his deputy, Pei Ji as chief clerk, Liu Chongli as marshal, and Linghu Defen as recorder.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之大悅，授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard of this he was greatly pleased and appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted when he heard of it and appointed Shentong Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從平京師，拜宗正卿。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of the capital and was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of the capital and was made Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，拜右翊衛大將軍，封永康王，尋改封淮安王，為山東道安撫大使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Yiwu Guard, enfeoffed as Prince of Yongkang, soon thereafter changed to Prince of Huai'an, and made Pacification Commissioner of the Shandong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 1 he was named General-in-Chief of the Right Yiwu Guard and created Prince of Yongkang; shortly afterward his title was changed to Prince of Huai'an, and he was appointed Pacification Commissioner for the Shandong circuit.

sentences.zh: 擊宇文化及於魏縣，化及不能抗，東走聊城。

translations.literal: He attacked Yu Wenhuaji at Wei County; Huaji could not resist and fled east to Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Yu Wenhuaji at Wei County; unable to hold, Huaji fled east toward Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 神通進兵躡之，至聊城。

translations.literal: Shentong pressed forward in pursuit and reached Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong pursued and came up to Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 會化及糧盡請降，神通不受。

translations.literal: When Huaji's provisions were exhausted he asked to surrender; Shentong would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji, his supplies exhausted, offered to surrender, but Shentong refused.

sentences.zh: 其副使黃門侍郎崔干勸納之，神通曰：「兵士暴露已久，賊計窮糧盡，克在旦暮，正當攻取，以示國威，散其玉帛，以為軍賞。

translations.literal: His deputy, Yellow Gate Attendant Cui Gan, urged him to accept the surrender. Shentong said: "The soldiers have been exposed to the elements for a long time; the rebels are at their wits' end and out of grain—victory is imminent. We should attack to display the state's might and distribute their valuables as rewards for the army.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy envoy, Yellow Gate Attendant Cui Gan, urged him to accept the surrender. Shentong replied: "Our men have been in the field far too long. The enemy is cornered and out of food—victory is only a matter of days. We ought to take the city by assault to show the empire's might and divide their treasure as booty for the troops.

sentences.zh: 若受降者，吾何以藉手乎？」

translations.literal: If we accept their surrender, how shall I reward my men?
translations.idiomatic: If we simply accept their surrender, what will there be left for my soldiers?

sentences.zh: 干曰：「今建德方至，化及未平，兩賊之間，事必危迫。

translations.literal: Gan said: "Dou Jiande is now approaching while Huaji is not yet subdued; caught between two foes, the situation will surely grow perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Gan said: "Dou Jiande is on his way while Huaji is still unconquered. Caught between two enemies, we will be in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 不攻而下之，此勳甚大。

translations.literal: To take the city without fighting would be a very great achievement.
translations.idiomatic: To bring the city over without a fight would be a signal achievement.

sentences.zh: 今貪其玉帛，敗無日矣！」

translations.literal: Now, if you covet their valuables, defeat will come any day!"
translations.idiomatic: If you grasp only for their treasure now, defeat will follow in no time!"

sentences.zh: 神通怒，囚干於軍中。

translations.literal: Shentong was angry and imprisoned Gan in the army camp.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong flew into a rage and had Gan thrown into the stockade.

sentences.zh: 既而士及自濟北饋之，化及軍稍振，遂拒戰。

translations.literal: Before long Shiji came from Jibei with supplies for him; Huaji's army gradually revived and they resisted battle.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shiji arrived from Jibei with provisions, Huaji's forces rallied somewhat, and they stood to fight.

sentences.zh: 神通督兵薄而擊之，貝州刺史趙君德攀堞而上，神通心害其功，因止軍不戰，君德大詬而下，城又堅守。

translations.literal: Shentong urged his troops forward in a close assault. Beizhou prefect Zhao Junde climbed the battlements, but Shentong, jealous of his merit, halted the army and would not fight; Junde cursed loudly and came down, and the city again held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong pressed the attack at close quarters. Zhao Junde, prefect of Beizhou, scaled the wall, but Shentong, resentful of another man's glory, ordered the army to stand down; Junde cursed him roundly and withdrew, and the city remained stubbornly defended.

sentences.zh: 神通乃分兵數千人往魏州取攻具，中路復為莘人所敗。

translations.literal: Shentong then detached several thousand men to go to Weizhou for siege equipment, but on the way they were again defeated by the people of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong then sent several thousand men to Weizhou for siege engines, but midway they were routed again by the men of Xin.

sentences.zh: 竇建德軍且至，遂引軍而退。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande's army was about to arrive, so he withdrew his forces.
translations.idiomatic: With Dou Jiande's army nearing, he drew off his troops.

sentences.zh: 後二日，化及為建德所虜，賊勢益張，山東城邑多歸建德。

translations.literal: Two days later Huaji was captured by Jiande; the rebel power grew stronger, and many cities of Shandong submitted to Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Huaji fell into Jiande's hands; rebel strength swelled, and town after town in Shandong went over to Jiande.

sentences.zh: 神通兵漸散，退保黎陽，依徐勣，俄為建德所陷。

translations.literal: Shentong's troops gradually dispersed; he fell back to defend Liyang, relying on Xu Ji, and soon was trapped by Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong's force melted away; he fell back to Liyang and threw in with Xu Ji, only to be overrun by Jiande shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 及建德敗，復授河北道行台尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, he was again appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs on the Hebei Expeditionary Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiande's defeat he was reappointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs on the Hebei expeditionary staff.

sentences.zh: 從太宗平劉黑闥，遷左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Taizong in pacifying Liu Heita and was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Wuwei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong in suppressing Liu Heita and was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Left Wuwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，拜開府儀同三司，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was appointed Defender of the Palace with the status of Three Excellencies and granted five hundred actual fief households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 1 he was made Defender of the Palace with the rank of Three Excellencies and granted an enfeoffment of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 時太宗謂諸功臣曰：「朕敘公等勳效，量定封邑，恐不能盡當，各自言。」

translations.literal: At that time Taizong said to the meritorious ministers: "I am reviewing your achievements and allotting fiefs; I fear I may not have judged them all fairly—speak for yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Taizong told his chief ministers: "I am ranking your achievements and assigning fiefs, but I may not have judged everyone fairly—tell me yourselves.

sentences.zh: 神通曰：「義旗初起，臣率兵先至，今房玄齡、杜如晦等刀筆之人，功居第一，臣且不服。」

translations.literal: Shentong said: "When the righteous banner first rose I led troops and arrived first; now Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and other men of the writing brush rank first in merit—I cannot accept it."
translations.idiomatic: Shentong said: "When the uprising began I was the first to bring troops in. Yet now Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and other desk-bound clerks stand first in merit—I cannot accept that."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「義旗初起，人皆有心。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When the righteous banner first rose, everyone had the same intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "When the uprising began, everyone had the same resolve.

sentences.zh: 叔父雖率兵先至，未嘗身履行陣。

translations.literal: Although Uncle led troops and arrived first, you never personally went into battle.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle, you may have brought troops in early, but you never once took the field yourself.

sentences.zh: 山東未定，受委專征，建德南侵，全軍陷沒；

translations.literal: When Shandong was still unsettled you were entrusted with independent command; when Jiande invaded from the south your entire army was lost;
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong was still unsettled you were given independent command, yet when Jiande swept south your whole army was wiped out;

sentences.zh: 及劉黑闥翻動，叔父望風而破。

translations.literal: and when Liu Heita rebelled, Uncle collapsed at the mere sight of the enemy wind.
translations.idiomatic: and when Liu Heita rose again, you broke and ran at the first sight of trouble.

sentences.zh: 今計勳行賞，玄齡等有籌謀帷幄定社稷功，所以漢之蕭何，雖無汗馬，指縱推轂，故功居第一。

translations.literal: Now, in reckoning merit and bestowing rewards, Xuanling and the others have the achievement of planning within the tent and settling the altars of state; like the Han's Xiao He, though without sweat of horse, they directed from the chariot and pushed the wheel—therefore their merit ranks first.
translations.idiomatic: In weighing merit and granting rewards today, Xuanling and his fellows earned their place by plotting within the command tent and securing the realm—like the Han minister Xiao He, who won no glory in the saddle yet steered the chariot from behind. That is why they stand first.

sentences.zh: 叔父於國至親，誠無所愛，必不可緣私濫與勳臣同賞耳。」

translations.literal: Uncle is the closest of kin to the state and I truly hold nothing back from you, but you certainly cannot, for private reasons, be indiscriminately rewarded on a par with the meritorious ministers."
translations.idiomatic: You are my closest kinsman and I withhold nothing from you in affection, but you surely cannot expect to be heaped with the same rewards as the men who earned them—merely because we are kin."

sentences.zh: 四年，薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he died.

sentences.zh: 太宗為之廢朝，贈司空，謚曰靖。

translations.literal: Taizong suspended court for him, posthumously appointed him Minister of Works, and gave him the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong canceled court in mourning, posthumously created him Minister of Works, and gave him the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔與河間王孝恭、贈陝州大行台右僕射鄖節公殷開山、贈民部尚書渝襄公劉政會配饗高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict ordered that he, together with Prince of Hejian Xiaogong, the posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Yun Jie Yin Kaishan (Right Vice Director of the Shaanzhou Grand Expeditionary Headquarters), and the posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Yu Xiang Liu Zhenghui (Minister of the Ministry of Population), receive joint sacrifice in Gaozu's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 an edict directed that he share sacrifice in Gaozu's temple hall with Prince of Hejian Xiaogong, the posthumously honored Duke of Yun Jie Yin Kaishan, and the posthumously honored Duke of Yu Xiang Liu Zhenghui.

sentences.zh: 有子十一人：長子道彥，武德五年，封膠東王；

translations.literal: He had eleven sons: the eldest, Daoyan, was in the fifth year of Wude enfeoffed as Prince of Jiaodong;
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons. The eldest, Daoyan, was created Prince of Jiaodong in Wude year 5;

sentences.zh: 次孝察，高密王；

translations.literal: next Xiaocha, Prince of Gaomi;
translations.idiomatic: next came Xiaocha, Prince of Gaomi;

sentences.zh: 孝同，淄川王；

translations.literal: Xiaotong, Prince of Zichuan;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong, Prince of Zichuan;

sentences.zh: 孝慈，廣平王；

translations.literal: Xiaoci, Prince of Guangping;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci, Prince of Guangping;

sentences.zh: 孝友，河間王；

translations.literal: Xiaoyou, Prince of Hejian;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou, Prince of Hejian;

sentences.zh: 孝節，清河王；

translations.literal: Xiaojie, Prince of Qinghe;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojie, Prince of Qinghe;

sentences.zh: 孝義，膠西王。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi, Prince of Jiaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: and Xiaoyi, Prince of Jiaoxi.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖受禪，以天下未定，廣封宗室以威天下，皇從弟及侄年始孩童者數十人，皆封為郡王。

translations.literal: At first, when Gaozu received the abdication, because the realm was not yet settled he broadly enfeoffed the imperial clan to overawe the world; several dozen of the emperor's cousins and nephews who were still children were all enfeoffed as princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Gaozu took the throne the realm was still unsettled, so he enfeoffed the imperial clan on a wide scale to overawe the empire; dozens of his cousins and nephews who were still mere children were all created princes of commanderies.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，因舉宗正屬藉問侍臣曰：「遍封宗子，於天下便乎？」

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he had the Director of the Imperial Clan present the genealogical register and asked his attendants: "Is it convenient for the realm to enfeoff every clansman?
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne he had the Director of the Imperial Clan bring out the genealogical register and asked his ministers: "Does it serve the realm to enfeoff every member of the clan?

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射封德彝對曰：「歷觀往古，封王者，今最為多。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Feng Deyi replied: "Looking through past ages, the enfeoffed kings of today are the most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Feng Deyi answered: "Looking back through history, never have there been so many enfeoffed kings as today.

sentences.zh: 兩漢已降，唯封帝子及親兄弟，若宗室疏遠者，非有大功如周之郇、滕，漢之賈、澤，並不得濫封，所以別親疏也。

translations.literal: From the two Han dynasties onward, only the emperor's sons and full brothers were enfeoffed; if distant members of the clan had no great achievement like the Zhou's Xun and Teng or the Han's Jia and Ze, they were not indiscriminately enfeoffed—this was how near and distant kin were distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: From the two Han dynasties on, only the emperor's own sons and full brothers were enfeoffed as kings; more distant clansmen, unless they had earned distinction like the Zhou states of Xun and Teng or the Han marquisates of Jia and Ze, were not enfeoffed indiscriminately—that was how near and distant kin were kept apart.

sentences.zh: 先朝惇睦九族，一切封王，爵命既隆，多給力役，蓋以天下為私，殊非至公馭物之道。」

translations.literal: The previous court, in showing affection to the nine degrees of kin, enfeoffed them all as kings; once rank was exalted, many were given corvée labor—this treated the realm as private property and was far from the utmost impartial way of governing things."
translations.idiomatic: The previous reign, in the name of cherishing the nine degrees of kin, enfeoffed them all as kings; once their titles were raised so high, they drew heavily on corvée labor. That was treating the empire as a family possession, not the impartial way to govern the realm."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「朕理天下，本為百姓，非欲勞百姓以養己之親也。」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "I govern the realm fundamentally for the common people; I do not wish to burden the common people to support my own kin."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "I govern the realm for the sake of the people, not to burden the people in order to sustain my own relatives."

sentences.zh: 於是宗室率以屬疏降爵為郡公，唯有功者數十人封王。

translations.literal: Thereupon the imperial clan, for the most part because of distant kinship, were reduced in rank to dukes of commanderies; only several dozen with achievement were enfeoffed as kings.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the imperial clan, for the most part on grounds of distant kinship, were reduced to dukes of commanderies; only several dozen men with real merit retained princely titles.

sentences.zh: 是時道彥等並隨例降爵。

translations.literal: At that time Daoyan and the others all followed the precedent and were reduced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Daoyan and his brothers were all reduced in rank under the same rule.

sentences.zh: 道彥與季弟孝逸最知名。

translations.literal: Daoyan and his youngest brother Xiaoyi were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Among them Daoyan and his youngest brother Xiaoyi were the best known.

sentences.zh: 道彥幼而事親甚謹。

translations.literal: Daoyan from youth served his parents with great care.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Daoyan served his parents with exceptional devotion.

sentences.zh: 初，義師起，神通逃難，被疾於山谷，綿曆數旬，山中食盡。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the righteous army rose, Shentong fled into hiding; he fell ill in the mountains and ravines for several tens of days until food in the hills was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began, Shentong went into hiding; he fell ill in the mountains and lingered there for weeks until the food in the hills was gone.

sentences.zh: 道彥著故弊衣，出人間乞丐，及采野實，以供其父，身無所啖。

translations.literal: Daoyan wore old, worn-out clothes, went among the people as a beggar, and gathered wild fruits to supply his father, eating nothing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan put on ragged old clothes, went among the villages as a beggar, and gathered wild fruit to feed his father, keeping nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 其父分以食之，輒詐言已啖，而覆藏留之，以備闕乏。

translations.literal: When his father shared food with him, he would falsely say he had already eaten and secretly hoard what was left against future want.
translations.idiomatic: When his father offered him a share, he would claim he had already eaten and quietly set food aside for the days ahead.

sentences.zh: 及神通應義舉，授朝請大夫。

translations.literal: When Shentong responded to the righteous rising, Daoyan was appointed Court Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: When Shentong joined the uprising, Daoyan was appointed Court Consultant.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，封義興郡公，進封膠東王，授隴州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing Commandery, advanced to Prince of Jiaodong, and appointed prefect of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Daoyan was created Duke of Yixing, then advanced to Prince of Jiaodong and appointed prefect of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，轉相州都督，例降爵為公，拜岷州都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was transferred to regional commander of Xiangzhou; by precedent his rank was reduced to duke, and he was appointed regional commander of Minzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era he was made regional commander of Xiangzhou; under the general reduction of titles he became a duke and was appointed regional commander of Minzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，廬於墓側，負土成墳，躬植松柏，容貌哀毀，親友皆不復識之。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he built a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to form the mound, personally planted pines and cypresses, and his appearance was so wasted by grief that kin and friends could no longer recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he lived in a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to raise the mound, and planted pines and cypresses with his own hands; grief so wasted his face that friends and kin could scarcely recognize him.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而嘉嘆，令侍中王珪就加開喻。

translations.literal: Taizong heard of this, praised and sighed over it, and ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Gui to go and offer further consolation and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong heard of it, praised him warmly, and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Gui to comfort and counsel him.

sentences.zh: 復授岷州都督。

translations.literal: He was again appointed regional commander of Minzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed regional commander of Minzhou.

sentences.zh: 道彥遣使告喻党項諸部，申國威靈，多有降附。

translations.literal: Daoyan sent envoys to announce and instruct the various Tangut tribes, proclaiming the state's majesty and authority; many submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan sent envoys to announce the empire's authority to the Tangut tribes, and many submitted.

sentences.zh: 李靖之擊吐谷渾也，詔道彥為赤水道行軍總管。

translations.literal: When Li Jing attacked Tuyuhun, an edict appointed Daoyan Grand Commander of the Chishui Circuit Expeditionary Force.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing marched against Tuyuhun, an edict named Daoyan Grand Commander of the Chishui Circuit expedition.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷復厚幣遺党項，令為鄉導，党項首領拓拔赤辭來詣靖軍，請諸將曰：「往者隋人來擊吐谷渾，我党項每資軍用，而隋人無信，必見侵掠。

translations.literal: At that time the court again sent rich gifts to the Tangut and ordered them to serve as guides; the Tangut leader Tuoba Chici came to Jing's army and addressed the generals: "In the past when the Sui came to attack Tuyuhun, we Tangut always supplied the army's needs, yet the Sui were faithless and invariably plundered us.
translations.idiomatic: The court again sent rich gifts to the Tangut and asked them to serve as guides. The Tangut leader Tuoba Chici came to Jing's camp and told the generals: "Whenever the Sui marched against Tuyuhun we Tangut supplied their armies, yet the Sui were faithless and always turned to plunder.

sentences.zh: 今將軍若無他心者，我當資給糧運；

translations.literal: If the general now has no other intent, we shall supply grain transport;
translations.idiomatic: If you mean us no harm, we will furnish grain and transport;

sentences.zh: 如或我欺，當即固險以塞軍路。」

translations.literal: but if you deceive us, we shall at once hold the passes and block the army's road.
translations.idiomatic: but if you betray us, we will hold the passes and block your road at once.

sentences.zh: 諸將與之歃血而盟，赤辭信之。

translations.literal: The generals drank blood with him in alliance, and Chici trusted them.
translations.idiomatic: The generals drank blood with him in alliance, and Chici believed them.

sentences.zh: 道彥既至闊水，見赤辭無備，遂襲之，虜牛羊數千頭。

translations.literal: When Daoyan reached Kuoshui and saw Chici unguarded, he suddenly attacked and captured several thousand head of cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoyan reached the Kuoshui River and found Chici unprepared, he launched a surprise raid and seized several thousand head of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 於是諸羌怨怒，屯兵野狐硤，道彥不能進，為赤辭所乘，軍大敗，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various Qiang were resentful and angry, massed troops at Yehu Gorge; Daoyan could not advance, was taken advantage of by Chici, and his army suffered a great defeat with tens of thousands dead.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang tribes were enraged and massed at Yehu Gorge; Daoyan could not advance, Chici seized the moment, and his army was shattered—tens of thousands died.

sentences.zh: 道彥退保松州，竟坐減死徙邊。

translations.literal: Daoyan fell back to defend Songzhou and in the end, by statute, had his death sentence commuted to banishment to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan fell back to Songzhou and was eventually spared execution and banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 後起為涼州都督，尋卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled and appointed regional commander of Liangzhou; he soon died and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as regional commander of Liangzhou, died soon afterward, and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 孝逸少好學，解屬文。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi from youth loved learning and was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi was studious from youth and skilled at composition.

sentences.zh: 初封梁郡公。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 高宗末，歷給事中，四遷益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: At the end of Gaozong's reign he served successively as Supervising Censor and, after four promotions, as chief administrator of the Yizhou Grand Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Gaozong's reign he rose through the post of Supervising Censor to chief administrator of the Yizhou Grand Protectorate after four promotions.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，入為左衛將軍，甚見親遇。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu held court he entered service as General of the Left Guard and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian took power he entered court as General of the Left Guard and won her special favor.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，徐敬業據揚州作亂，以孝逸為左玉鈐衛大將軍、揚州行軍大總管，督軍以討之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhe, Xu Jingye seized Yangzhou and rebelled; Xiaoyi was made General-in-Chief of the Left Jade Bell Guard and Grand Commander of the Yangzhou Expeditionary Force to supervise the army in suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangzhe year 1, when Xu Jingye seized Yangzhou and rose in revolt, Xiaoyi was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Jade Bell Guard and Grand Commander of the Yangzhou expedition to lead the suppression.

sentences.zh: 孝逸引軍至淮，而敬業方南攻潤州，遣其弟敬猷屯兵淮陰；

translations.literal: Xiaoyi led his army to the Huai, while Jingye was then attacking Runzhou to the south and had sent his younger brother Jingyou to encamp at Huaiyin;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi marched to the Huai while Jingye was pressing south against Runzhou and had posted his brother Jingyou at Huaiyin;

sentences.zh: 偽將韋超據都梁山，以拒孝逸。

translations.literal: the rebel general Wei Chao held Duliang Mountain to resist Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: the rebel general Wei Chao held Duliang Mountain to block Xiaoyi's advance.

sentences.zh: 裨將馬敬臣擊斬賊之別帥尉遲昭、夏侯瓚等，超乃擁眾憑山以自固。

translations.literal: Lieutenant general Ma Jingchen attacked and beheaded the rebels' detached commanders Yuchi Zhao, Xiahou Zan, and others; Chao then gathered his followers and relied on the mountain to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant general Ma Jingchen attacked and killed the rebel detachments under Yuchi Zhao and Xiahou Zan; Chao then massed his men on the mountain and dug in.

sentences.zh: 或謂孝逸曰：「超眾守險，且憑山為阻，攻之則士無所施其力，騎無所騁其足，窮寇殊死，殺傷必眾。

translations.literal: Someone said to Xiaoyi: "Chao's host holds the passes and relies on the mountain as a barrier; if we attack, the infantry cannot exert their strength and the cavalry cannot stretch their legs—a cornered foe will fight to the death and casualties will surely be heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Xiaoyi: "Chao holds the heights and the mountain blocks us. If we assault, the foot soldiers cannot use their strength and the cavalry cannot deploy—a cornered enemy will fight to the death and our losses will be heavy.

sentences.zh: 不若分兵守之，大軍直趣揚州，未數日，其勢必降也。」

translations.literal: Better to detach troops to contain him while the main army presses straight for Yangzhou; within a few days their force will surely surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Better to leave a detachment to pin him while the main force strikes straight for Yangzhou—in a few days their whole cause will collapse.

sentences.zh: 支度使、廣府司馬薛克構曰：「超雖據險，其卒非多，今逢小寇不擊，何以示武？

translations.literal: Supply commissioner and Guangfu marshal Xue Kegou said: "Although Chao holds the passes, his troops are not numerous; if we meet a small bandit and do not strike, how shall we display martial prowess?
translations.idiomatic: Supply commissioner Xue Kegou said: "Chao may hold the heights, but his force is small. If we shrink from a minor foe, how will we show our mettle?

sentences.zh: 若加兵以守，則有闕前機；

translations.literal: If we add troops to hold him, we shall miss the prior opportunity;
translations.idiomatic: If we tie up troops to watch him, we miss our chance;

sentences.zh: 舍之而前，則終為後患，不如擊之。

translations.literal: if we leave him and advance, he will in the end be a later calamity—better to attack.
translations.idiomatic: if we pass him by he will plague us later. We ought to attack.

sentences.zh: 克超則淮陰自懾，淮陰破，則楚州諸縣必開門而候官軍。

translations.literal: If Chao is overcome, Huaiyin will itself be overawed; if Huaiyin falls, the counties of Chuzhou will surely open their gates and await the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat Chao and Huaiyin will quake; take Huaiyin and the counties of Chuzhou will open their gates to us.

sentences.zh: 然後進兵高郵，直趣江都，逆豎之首，可指掌而懸也。」

translations.literal: Then advance the army to Gaoyou and press straight for Jiangdu—the rebel chieftain's head can be hung at one's fingertips."
translations.idiomatic: Then march on Gaoyou and straight for Jiangdu—the rebel leader's head will be ours to take."

sentences.zh: 孝逸從其言，進兵擊超賊，眾壓伏，官軍登山急擊之，殺數百人，日暮圍解，超銜枚夜遁。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi followed his advice, advanced and attacked Chao's rebels; the host pressed them down, the imperial army climbed the mountain and struck urgently, killing several hundred; at dusk the siege was lifted and Chao gagged his men's mouths and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi took his advice, advanced against Chao, and pressed the rebels down the slope; the imperial troops stormed the height and killed several hundred. At dusk the encirclement broke, and Chao slipped away in silence that night.

sentences.zh: 孝逸引兵擊淮陰，大破敬猷之眾。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi led his troops to attack Huaiyin and inflicted a great defeat on Jingyou's force.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi marched on Huaiyin and routed Jingyou's army.

sentences.zh: 時敬業回軍屯於下阿溪以拒官軍，有流星墜其營。

translations.literal: At that time Jingye turned his army back and encamped at Xia'a Creek to resist the imperial army; a meteor fell into his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye then drew back and encamped at Xia'a Creek to face the imperial army, and a meteor fell into his camp.

sentences.zh: 孝逸引兵渡溪以擊之。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi led his troops across the creek to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi crossed the creek and attacked.

sentences.zh: 敬業初勝後敗，孝逸乘勝追奔數十里，敬業窘迫，與其黨攜妻子逃入海曲。

translations.literal: Jingye was first victorious then defeated; Xiaoyi, riding the victory, pursued in flight for several tens of li; Jingye was hard pressed and, with his partisans, fled with wives and children to the sea's bend.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye won the opening clash but was beaten afterward; Xiaoyi pressed the pursuit for miles. Hard pressed, Jingye fled with his followers, wives, and children toward the coast.

sentences.zh: 孝逸進據揚州，盡捕斬敬業等，振旅而還，以功進授鎮軍大將軍，轉左豹韜衛大將軍，改封吳國公。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi advanced and seized Yangzhou, captured and executed Jingye and the rest, shook out his ranks and returned; for his merit he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Leopard Bow Guard, and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Wu state.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi advanced into Yangzhou, captured and executed Jingye and his followers, and returned in triumph. For his service he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Leopard Bow Guard, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wu.

sentences.zh: 孝逸素有名望，自是時譽益重，武承嗣等深所忌嫉，數讒毀之。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi had long enjoyed renown; from this time his contemporary reputation grew even weightier; Wu Chengsi and others deeply envied and resented him and repeatedly slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi had long enjoyed a high reputation, and from this victory his standing grew even greater. Wu Chengsi and his faction deeply envied him and repeatedly slandered him.

sentences.zh: 垂拱二年，左遷施州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuigong, he was demoted to prefect of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: In 686 he was demoted to prefect of Shi.

sentences.zh: 其冬，承嗣等又使人誣告孝逸往任益州，嘗自解「逸」字云：「走繞兔者，常在月中。

translations.literal: That winter, Chengsi and others again sent men to falsely accuse Xiaoyi: during his earlier tenure in Yizhou he had once explained the character for Yi, saying, "One who runs circling a rabbit is always in the moon.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Chengsi and his allies sent men to accuse Xiaoyi falsely. They claimed that while governing Yizhou he had once parsed the yi of his own name, saying that to run after a rabbit is always to dwell in the moon — a pun on the character's components.

sentences.zh: 月既近天，合有天分。」

translations.literal: The moon being close to heaven, he ought to possess a heavenly portion."
translations.idiomatic: Since the moon stands near heaven, he was therefore claiming a mandate destined for the throne.

sentences.zh: 則天以孝逸常有功，減死配徙儋州，尋卒。

translations.literal: Empress Wu, because Xiaoyi had often rendered merit, commuted death to exile at Dan prefecture; soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, because Xiaoyi had often rendered great service, commuted his death sentence to exile in Dan prefecture. He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，贈益州大都督。

translations.literal: Early in Jingyun, he was posthumously appointed metropolitan overseer of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingyun era he was posthumously appointed metropolitan overseer of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 孝銳孫齊物，孝同曾孫國貞，別有傳。

translations.literal: Xiaorui's grandson Qiwu and Xiaotong's great-grandson Guozhen each have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: The biographies of Xiaorui's grandson Qiwu and Xiaotong's great-grandson Guozhen appear elsewhere in the work.

sentences.zh: 襄邑王神符，神通弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu was Shentong's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu, Prince of Xiangyi, was the younger brother of Prince Huai'an Shentong.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事兄以友悌聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he was known for treating his elder brother with friendship and fraternal respect.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was known for the friendship and fraternal devotion he showed his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 義寧初，授光祿大夫，封安吉郡公。

translations.literal: Early in Yining, he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Anji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yining era he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Anji commandery.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，進封襄邑郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, he was advanced to Prince of Xiangyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 he was promoted to Prince of Xiangyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 四年，累遷并州總管。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, after successive promotions he became area commander of Bing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 621, after a series of promotions, he became area commander of Bing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利可汗率眾來寇，神符出兵與戰於汾水東，敗之，斬首五百級，虜其馬二千匹。

translations.literal: The Türk khagan Jieli led his host to raid; Shenfu deployed troops and fought east of the Fen River, defeated them, took five hundred heads, and captured two thousand of their horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türk khagan Jieli led a raid, Shenfu took the field and fought him east of the Fen River. He routed the Türks, took five hundred heads, and captured two thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 又戰於沙河之北，獲其乙利達官並可汗所乘馬及甲獻之，由是召拜太府卿。

translations.literal: Again he fought north of the Sha River, captured their elite commander Yili and the khagan's own horse and armor, which he presented; for this he was summoned and appointed Director of the Palace Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again north of the Sha River, captured the Türk elite commander Yili along with the khagan's horse and armor, and presented them as trophies. He was then summoned to court and appointed Director of the Palace Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷揚州大都督，移州府及居人自丹陽渡江，州人賴焉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to metropolitan overseer of Yang prefecture; he moved the prefectural seat and its residents across the river from Danyang — the people of the prefecture relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: In 626 he was transferred to metropolitan overseer of Yang prefecture. He moved the prefectural seat and its residents across the river from Danyang, to the great benefit of the region.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，再遷宗正卿。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, he was again transferred to Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era he was again transferred, becoming Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 後以疾辭職，太宗幸其第問疾，賜以縑帛，每給羊酒。

translations.literal: Later he resigned office because of illness; Emperor Taizong visited his residence to inquire after his illness, bestowed silk and brocade on him, and regularly supplied mutton and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Later he resigned because of illness. Emperor Taizong visited his home to inquire after him, bestowed silk and brocade, and regularly sent mutton and wine.

sentences.zh: 又令乘小輿，引入紫微殿，以神符腳疾，乃遣三衛輿之而升。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to ride in a small palanquin and was brought into the Ziwei Hall; because Shenfu had foot ailment, the Three Guards were sent to carry him in a litter up the steps.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to ride in a small palanquin and was brought into the Ziwei Hall. Because Shenfu suffered from a foot ailment, the Three Guards carried him up in a litter.

sentences.zh: 尋授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was granted the ceremonial rank of Defender of the Palace with Privileges Equal to Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was granted the ceremonial rank of Grand Master with Privileges Equal to Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年薨，年七十三，贈司空、荊州都督，陪葬獻陵，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he died at age seventy-three; posthumously appointed Minister of Works and commissioner of Jing prefecture, buried with Xian mausoleum, posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 651 at the age of seventy-three. He was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and commissioner of Jing prefecture, buried with Emperor Gaozu's Xian mausoleum, and given the posthumous title Gong, Respectful.

sentences.zh: 有子七人，武德初，並封郡王，後例降封縣公。

translations.literal: He had seven sons; early in Wude all were enfeoffed as commandery princes, then by precedent demoted to county marquises.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons. Early in Wude all were enfeoffed as commandery princes, then later demoted by precedent to county marquises.

sentences.zh: 次子德懋、少子文暕最知名。

translations.literal: His second son Demao and youngest son Wenliang were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Of them his second son Demao and youngest son Wenliang were the best known.

sentences.zh: 德懋官至少府監、臨川郡公。

translations.literal: Demao rose to Director of the Lesser Treasury and Duke of Linchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Demao rose to serve as Director of the Lesser Treasury and Duke of Linchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 文暕歷幽州都督、魏郡公。

translations.literal: Wenliang served in turn as commissioner of You prefecture and Duke of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wenliang served in turn as commissioner of You prefecture and as Duke of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，坐事貶為藤州別駕，尋被誅。

translations.literal: During Chuigong, for an offense he was demoted to deputy prefect of Teng prefecture; soon afterward he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era he was demoted to deputy prefect of Teng prefecture for an offense and was soon executed.

sentences.zh: 文暕子佺，開元中為宗正卿。

translations.literal: Wenliang's son Quan, during Kaiyuan, served as Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Wenliang's son Quan served as Director of the Imperial Clan Court during the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 子孝協嗣，武德五年，封范陽郡王。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoxie succeeded; in the fifth year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Fanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoxie succeeded him. In 622 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Fanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，以屬疏例降封郇國公，累遷魏州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, by the precedent for distant kin his rank was reduced to Duke of Xun state; after successive promotions he became prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era, by the precedent for more distant imperial kin, his rank was reduced to Duke of Xun. He later rose through successive promotions to prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 麟德中，坐受贓賜死。

translations.literal: During Linde, for accepting bribes he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: During the Linde era he was sentenced to death for accepting bribes.

sentences.zh: 孝協弟孝斌，官至原州都督府長史。

translations.literal: Xiaoxie's younger brother Xiaobin rose to chief administrator of the Yuan prefecture commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxie's younger brother Xiaobin rose to serve as chief administrator of the Yuan prefecture commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 孝斌子思訓，高宗時累轉江都令。

translations.literal: Xiaobin's son Sixun, during Emperor Gaozong's reign, rose through successive transfers to magistrate of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobin's son Sixun, during Emperor Gaozong's reign, rose through successive appointments to magistrate of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 屬則天革命，宗室多見搆陷，思訓遂棄官潛匿。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu changed the dynasty, many of the imperial clan were framed and trapped; Sixun then resigned his office and went into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu seized power, many members of the imperial clan were framed. Sixun resigned his office and went into hiding.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，中宗初復宗社，以思訓舊齒，驟遷宗正卿，封隴西郡公，實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong, when Emperor Zhongzong first restored the state altars, because Sixun was a senior member of the clan he was suddenly promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan Court, enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi commandery with two hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era, when Emperor Zhongzong restored the Tang dynasty, Sixun was suddenly promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan Court and enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi commandery with an income of two hundred households, in recognition of his senior standing in the clan.

sentences.zh: 歷益州長史。

translations.literal: He served as chief administrator of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as chief administrator of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 開元初，左羽林大將軍，進封彭國公，更加實封二百戶，尋轉右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, he was General of the Left Forest Guard, advanced to Duke of Peng state with an additional two hundred taxable households, soon transferred to General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he was General of the Left Forest Guard, then promoted to Duke of Peng with an additional two hundred taxable households, and soon transferred to General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 開元六年卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 718.

sentences.zh: 贈秦州都督，陪葬橋陵。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed commissioner of Qin prefecture, buried with Qiao mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed commissioner of Qin prefecture and buried with Emperor Ruizong's Qiao mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 思訓尤善丹青，迄今繪事者推李將軍山水。

translations.literal: Sixun was especially skilled at painting; to this day painters praise General Li's landscape art.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun was especially skilled at painting. To this day painters speak of "General Li's landscapes" — the style he himself made famous.

sentences.zh: 思訓弟思誨，垂拱中揚州參軍。

translations.literal: Sixun's younger brother Sihui, during Chuigong, was an aide in Yang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun's younger brother Sihui served as an aide in Yang prefecture during the Chuigong era.

sentences.zh: 思誨子林甫別有傳。

translations.literal: Sihui's son Linpu has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Sihui's son Linpu appears separately in the work.

sentences.zh: 叔良弟德良，少有疾，不仕。

translations.literal: Shuliang's younger brother Deliang had illness from youth and did not serve in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang's younger brother Deliang had been ill from youth and never held office.

sentences.zh: 武德初，封新興王。

translations.literal: Early in Wude, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十一年薨，贈涼州都督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhenguan he died; posthumously appointed commissioner of Liang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 637 and was posthumously appointed commissioner of Liang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德良孫晉，先天中，為殿中監，兼雍州長史，甚有威名，紹封新興王。

translations.literal: Deliang's grandson Jin, during Xiantian, served as Director of the Palace Administration and concurrent chief administrator of Yong prefecture; he enjoyed great renown and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Deliang's grandson Jin, during the Xiantian era, served as Director of the Palace Administration and concurrent chief administrator of Yong prefecture. He enjoyed great renown and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 尋坐附會太平公主伏誅，改姓厲氏。

translations.literal: Soon afterward for associating with Princess Taiping he was executed; his surname was changed to Li.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was executed for associating with Princess Taiping, and his clan surname was changed to Li.

sentences.zh: 初，晉之就誅，僚吏皆奔散，唯司功李捴步從，不失在官之禮，仍哭其屍。

translations.literal: When Jin was about to be executed, his staff officials all fled; only Records Officer Li Zong followed on foot, never failing the decorum of office, and still wept over his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was about to be executed, his staff officials all fled. Only Records Officer Li Zong followed on foot, observing every propriety of office, and wept over his corpse.

sentences.zh: 姚崇聞之曰：「欒、向之儔也。」

translations.literal: Yao Chong heard of this and said: "A companion of Luan and Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chong heard of this, he said, "He is of the same breed as Luan and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 擢為尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to a Secretariat Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong had him promoted to a Secretariat officer.

sentences.zh: 後官至澤州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he rose to prefect of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to serve as prefect of Ze.

sentences.zh: 德良弟幼良，武德初，封長樂王。

translations.literal: Deliang's younger brother Youliang, early in Wude, was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Deliang's younger brother Youliang was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle early in Wude.

sentences.zh: 時有人盜其馬者，幼良獲盜而閃殺之，高祖怒曰：「昔人賜盜馬者酒，終獲其報，爾輒行戮，何無古風！

translations.literal: Once when someone stole his horse, Youliang captured the thief and killed him on the spot; Emperor Gaozu was angry and said: "In olden days men gave wine to one who stole their horses, and in the end received repayment — you rashly carried out execution; where is the ancient spirit!
translations.idiomatic: Once when someone stole his horse, Youliang captured the thief and killed him on the spot. Emperor Gaozu was furious and said, "In antiquity a man who had his horse stolen would treat the thief to wine and in the end receive his reward. You executed the man outright — where is the spirit of the ancients!

sentences.zh: 盜者信有罪矣，專殺豈非枉邪？」

translations.literal: A thief is indeed guilty — but is summary killing not injustice?
translations.idiomatic: The thief was indeed guilty, but is summary execution not itself a wrong?

sentences.zh: 遣禮部尚書李綱於朝堂集宗室王公而撻之。

translations.literal: He sent Minister of Rites Li Gang to assemble the princes and nobles of the imperial clan in the court hall and have him flogged.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Minister of Rites Li Gang to assemble the princes and nobles of the imperial clan in the court hall and have Youliang flogged.

sentences.zh: 自後累遷涼州都督，嘗引不逞百餘人為左右，多侵暴市裡，行旅苦之。

translations.literal: Afterward he rose through successive transfers to commissioner of Liang prefecture; he once retained more than a hundred unruly men as his close retainers, who frequently plundered the markets — travelers suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he rose through successive appointments to commissioner of Liang prefecture. He kept more than a hundred unruly men as personal retainers, and they frequently terrorized the markets. Travelers suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，有告幼良陰養死士，交通境外，恐謀為反叛，詔遣中書令宇文士及代為都督，並按其事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, someone reported that Youliang secretly nurtured desperate fighters, maintained contact beyond the border, and might plot rebellion; an edict sent Chief Councillor Yuwen Shiji to replace him as commissioner and investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, someone reported that Youliang was secretly training desperate men and maintaining contacts beyond the border, possibly plotting rebellion. An edict sent Chief Councillor Yuwen Shiji to replace him as commissioner and investigate.

sentences.zh: 士及慮其為變，遂縊殺之。

translations.literal: Shiji feared he might rebel and strangled him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a revolt, Shiji had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 河間王孝恭，琛之弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Xiaogong was Chen's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hejian Xiaogong was the younger brother of Prince of Xiangwu Chen.

sentences.zh: 高祖克京師，拜左光祿大夫，尋為山南道招慰大使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took the capital, he was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; soon afterward he became commissioner for pacification of the South Mountain circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the capital, Xiaogong was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness. Soon afterward he became commissioner for pacification of the South Mountain circuit.

sentences.zh: 自金州出於巴蜀，招攜以禮，降附者三十餘州。

translations.literal: From Jin prefecture he proceeded into Ba-Shu, winning people over with courtesy; more than thirty prefectures submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Setting out from Jin prefecture into Ba and Shu, he won people over with courtesy, and more than thirty prefectures submitted.

sentences.zh: 孝恭進擊硃粲，破之，諸將曰：「此食人賊也，為害實深，請坑之。」

translations.literal: Xiaogong pressed the attack on Zhu Can and defeated him; the generals said: "These are man-eating bandits; the harm they do runs very deep — please execute them by burying alive.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong pressed the attack on Zhu Can and defeated him. The generals said, "These are man-eating bandits who have done terrible harm. We ask that they be buried alive.

sentences.zh: 孝恭曰：「不可！

translations.literal: Xiaogong said: "You must not!
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong said, "No!

sentences.zh: 自此已東，皆為寇境，若聞此事，豈有來降者乎？」

translations.literal: From here eastward all lies within bandit territory — if they hear of this, will there be any who come to surrender?"
translations.idiomatic: From here eastward all is enemy territory. If word of this spreads, who will dare to surrender?

sentences.zh: 盡赦而不殺，由是書檄所至，相繼降款。

translations.literal: He pardoned them all and did not kill them; thereafter wherever his proclamations reached, submissions followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned them all instead. Thereafter, wherever his proclamations reached, surrender followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，授信州總管，承製拜假。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, he was appointed area commander of Xin prefecture with authority to grant provisional commissions by imperial writ.
translations.idiomatic: In 619 he was appointed area commander of Xin prefecture with authority to grant provisional commissions under imperial writ.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑據江陵，孝恭獻平銑之策，高祖嘉納之。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian held Jiangling; Xiaogong submitted a plan to pacify Xian, and Emperor Gaozu praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xian held Jiangling, Xiaogong submitted a plan to defeat him, and Emperor Gaozu praised and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the third year his enfeoffment was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In 620 his title was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 改信州為夔州，使拜孝恭為總管，令大造舟楫，教習水戰，以圖蕭銑。

translations.literal: Xin prefecture was renamed Kui prefecture; Xiaogong was appointed its area commander, ordered to build ships in great numbers and drill naval warfare, with the aim of taking Xiao Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Xin prefecture was renamed Kui prefecture, and Xiaogong was appointed area commander there. He was ordered to build a large fleet and train his forces in naval warfare for a campaign against Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 孝恭召巴蜀首領子弟，量才授用，致之左右，外示引擢，而實以為質也。

translations.literal: Xiaogong summoned the sons of tribal leaders in Ba-Shu, appointed them according to their talents and kept them at his side; outwardly this showed promotion, but in fact they served as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong summoned the sons of Ba-Shu tribal leaders, assigned them posts suited to their abilities, and kept them close at hand. Outwardly it looked like promotion; in fact they were hostages.

sentences.zh: 尋授荊湘道行軍總管，統水陸十二總管，發自硤州，進軍江陵。

translations.literal: Soon he was made campaign commander of the Jing-Xiang circuit, commanding twelve area commanders by land and water; setting out from Xia prefecture, he marched on Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed campaign commander of the Jing-Xiang circuit, with twelve land and naval commanders under him. He set out from Xia prefecture and advanced on Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 攻其水城，克之，所得船散於江中。

translations.literal: He attacked their water fort and took it; the captured ships he scattered on the river.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed their river fort and took it, then scattered the captured ships down the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「虜得賊船，當藉其用，何為棄之，無乃資賊耶？」

translations.literal: All the generals said: "Capturing the rebel ships, we ought to make use of them — why abandon them? Will this not supply the bandits?
translations.idiomatic: The generals objected: "We should put those rebel ships to use. Why cast them away? Aren't we just handing the enemy an advantage?

sentences.zh: 孝恭曰：「不然，蕭銑偽境，南極嶺外，東至洞庭。

translations.literal: Xiaogong said: "Not so. Xiao Xian's rebel territory extends south to beyond the mountain ranges and east to Dongting.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong replied, "Not at all. Xiao Xian's rebel territory runs south to the far side of the Nanling ranges and east to Dongting.

sentences.zh: 若攻城未拔，援兵復到，我則內外受敵，進退不可，雖有舟楫，何所用之？

translations.literal: If the siege is not won and relief troops arrive again, we will be attacked inside and out, unable to advance or retreat — even with ships, of what use would they be?
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to take the city and their reinforcements arrive, we'll be caught between enemies with no room to advance or retreat. Even with ships, what good would they do us?

sentences.zh: 今銑緣江州鎮忽見船舸亂下，必知銑敗，未敢進兵，來去覘伺，動淹旬月，用緩其救，克之必矣。」

translations.literal: Now if the garrisons along the river suddenly see vessels drifting down in disorder, they will surely know Xian is defeated, will not dare advance, and will come and go spying and watching, delaying a full month or more — thus delaying their relief; victory is certain.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian's riverside garrisons see boats drifting downstream in disorder, they'll know he's lost and hesitate to advance. They'll linger on the river scouting for weeks—buying us time. Victory is assured.

sentences.zh: 銑救兵至巴陵，見船被江而下，果狐疑不敢輕進。

translations.literal: Xian's relief troops reached Baling; seeing ships spread across the river drifting downstream, they indeed grew suspicious and did not dare advance lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's relief force reached Baling, saw the scattered vessels floating downriver, and as Xiaogong had predicted, hung back in suspicion rather than press forward.

sentences.zh: 既內外阻絕，銑於是出降。

translations.literal: With communications inside and out cut off, Xian thereupon came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off both within and without, Xian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，拜孝恭荊州大總管，使畫工貌而視之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and appointed Xiaogong Grand Area Commander of Jing prefecture, having painters portray him for viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was delighted. He appointed Xiaogong Grand Area Commander of Jing prefecture and had painters render his likeness for the court to admire.

sentences.zh: 於是開置屯田，創立銅冶，百姓利焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened military colonies and established copper smelting; the common people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: He then established military colonies and copper works, to the benefit of the local populace.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷襄州道行台尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Left Vice President of the Xiangzhou Circuit Executive.
translations.idiomatic: In 623 he was made Left Vice President of the Xiangzhou Circuit Executive.

sentences.zh: 時荊襄雖定，嶺表尚未悉平。

translations.literal: At the time although Jing-Xiang was settled, the region south of the ranges was not yet fully pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jing and Xiang were now secure, the far south had not yet been fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 孝恭分遣使人撫慰，嶺南四十九州皆來款附。

translations.literal: Xiaogong sent envoys in separate directions to soothe and reassure; all forty-nine prefectures south of the ranges came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong dispatched envoys throughout the region to win hearts and minds. All forty-nine prefectures south of the Nanling submitted.

sentences.zh: 及輔公祏據江東反，發兵寇壽陽，命孝恭為行軍元帥以擊之。

translations.literal: When Fu Gongshi held Jiangdong in rebellion, raised troops and raided Shouyang, Xiaogong was ordered as campaign commander to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi seized Jiangdong and rebelled, sending raiders against Shouyang, Xiaogong was appointed supreme campaign commander to crush him.

sentences.zh: 七年，孝恭自荊州趣九江，時李靖、李勣、黃君漢、張鎮州、盧祖尚並受孝恭節度。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Xiaogong advanced from Jing prefecture toward Jiujiang; at that time Li Jing, Li Ji, Huang Junhan, Zhang Zhenzhou, and Lu Zushang all fell under Xiaogong's command.
translations.idiomatic: In 624 Xiaogong marched from Jing prefecture toward Jiujiang. Li Jing, Li Ji, Huang Junhan, Zhang Zhenzhou, and Lu Zushang all served under his command.

sentences.zh: 將發，與諸將宴集，命取水，忽變為血，在座者皆失色。

translations.literal: Just before setting out, at a banquet with the generals he ordered water brought; it suddenly turned to blood, and all present changed color.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of departure he banqueted his generals. When water was brought to the table it turned to blood. Every man present blanched.

sentences.zh: 孝恭舉止自若，徐諭之曰：「禍福無門，唯人所召。

translations.literal: Xiaogong carried himself as usual and slowly told them: "Fortune and disaster have no fixed door — only what men summon.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong remained composed. "Fortune and disaster have no fixed gate," he told them calmly. "They are only what men bring upon themselves.

sentences.zh: 自顧無負於物，諸公何見憂之深！

translations.literal: Considering myself, I have done nothing to wrong others — why do you gentlemen worry so deeply!
translations.idiomatic: I know I have wronged no one. Why are you so troubled?

sentences.zh: 公祏惡積禍盈，今承廟算以致討，碗中之血，乃公祏授首之後征。」

translations.literal: Gongshi's evil is piled up and his doom full; now we carry out the imperial plan to punish him — the blood in the bowl is an omen that Gongshi will lose his head after the campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi has piled up evil until disaster must fall. We march under the emperor's plan to destroy him. This blood in the bowl is an omen that Gongshi will lose his head when the campaign ends.

sentences.zh: 遂盡飲而罷。

translations.literal: Then he drank it all and ended the feast.
translations.idiomatic: He drained the cup and dismissed the gathering.

sentences.zh: 時人服其識度而能安眾。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his insight and composure in settling the troops.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it marveled at his poise and his ability to steady the troops.

sentences.zh: 公祏遣其偽將馮惠亮、陳當時領水軍屯於博望山，陳正通、徐紹宗率步騎軍於青林山。

translations.literal: Gongshi sent his rebel generals Feng Huiliang and Chen Dangshi to lead the navy and encamp on Bowang Mountain; Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong led infantry and cavalry at Qinglin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi posted his generals Feng Huiliang and Chen Dangshi with the fleet on Bowang Mountain, and Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong with infantry and cavalry on Qinglin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 孝恭至，堅壁不與斗，使奇兵斷其糧道。

translations.literal: When Xiaogong arrived, he strengthened his walls and would not give battle, sending surprise troops to cut off their supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong arrived and refused battle behind strengthened defenses while detachments severed the rebel supply lines.

sentences.zh: 賊漸饣委，夜薄我營，孝恭安臥不動。

translations.literal: The rebels gradually grew hungry and weakened; by night they drew near our camp, but Xiaogong lay calmly without moving.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels grew hungrier and weaker, they raided the camp by night. Xiaogong slept on undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 明日，縱羸兵以攻賊壘，使盧祖尚率精騎列陣以待之。

translations.literal: The next day he sent weak troops to attack the rebel fort, while having Lu Zushang lead elite cavalry drawn up in formation to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent weak troops to feint at the rebel fort while Lu Zushang waited with elite cavalry in formation.

sentences.zh: 俄而攻壘者敗走，賊出追奔數里，遇祖尚軍，與戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Before long the attackers on the fort fled in defeat; the rebels came out in pursuit for several li, met Zushang's army, joined battle, and were routed.
translations.idiomatic: The feinting force broke and fled. The rebels gave chase for several li, ran into Lu Zushang's cavalry, and were routed.

sentences.zh: 正通棄營而走，復與馮惠亮保梁山。

translations.literal: Zhengtong abandoned his camp and fled, joining Feng Huiliang again to hold Liang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong abandoned his camp and rejoined Feng Huiliang on Liang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 孝恭乘勝攻之，破其梁山別鎮，赴水死者數千人，正通率陸軍夜遁。

translations.literal: Xiaogong pressed the victory and attacked, breaking their separate fort at Liang Mountain; several thousand drowned in the water; Zhengtong led the land army in flight by night.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong pressed the attack, stormed the secondary fort on Liang Mountain, and killed several thousand rebels who drowned trying to escape. Zhengtong fled by night with the land forces.

sentences.zh: 總管李靖又下廣陵城，拔楊子鎮。

translations.literal: Area Commander Li Jing also took Guangling city and captured Yangzi garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing, area commander under Xiaogong, took Guangling and captured Yangzi garrison.

sentences.zh: 公祏窮蹙，棄丹陽東走。

translations.literal: Gongshi was hard pressed and abandoned Danyang, fleeing east.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Gongshi abandoned Danyang and fled east.

sentences.zh: 孝恭命騎將追之，至武康，擒公祏及其偽僕射西門君儀等數十人，致於麾下，江南悉平。

translations.literal: Xiaogong ordered cavalry to pursue; at Wukang they captured Gongshi and his rebel Secretariat Director Ximen Junyi and several dozen others, bringing them under command; all of Jiangnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong sent cavalry in pursuit. At Wukang they captured Gongshi, his chancellor Ximen Junyi, and dozens of other rebels. Jiangnan was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 璽書褒賞，賜甲第一區、女樂二部、奴婢七百人、金寶珍玩甚眾，授東南道行台尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: An imperial edict commended and rewarded him, granting one set of armor, two troupes of female musicians, seven hundred slaves and maidservants, and a great many gold treasures and precious curios; he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing for the Southeast Circuit Executive Office.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent an edict of commendation, along with a suit of armor, two companies of female musicians, seven hundred servants, and a lavish array of gold and precious objects. Xiaogong was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Southeast Circuit executive staff.

sentences.zh: 後廢行台，拜揚州大都督。

translations.literal: Later the executive office was abolished, and he was appointed Grand Area Commander of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the executive office was later abolished, he was appointed grand area commander of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝恭既破公祏，江淮及嶺南皆統攝之。

translations.literal: After Xiaogong had defeated Gongshi, he governed and commanded all of the Jiang-Huai region and Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiaogong had crushed Gongshi, he held authority over the Jiang-Huai heartland and all of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 自大業末，群雄競起，皆為太宗所平，謀臣猛將並在麾下，罕有別立勳庸者，唯孝恭著方面之功，聲名甚盛。

translations.literal: From the end of the Daye reign, rival heroes rose in competition; all were pacified by Taizong; strategists and fierce generals were all under his command; rarely did anyone establish separate feats of merit—only Xiaogong achieved merit in a regional command, and his fame was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Since the turmoil at the close of the Daye era, every rival warlord had risen only to be brought down by Taizong. His strategists and battle-hardened generals served under one banner, and few won independent glory. Xiaogong alone earned distinction as a regional commander, and his renown stood very high.

sentences.zh: 厚自崇重，欲以威名鎮遠，築宅於石頭，陳廬徼以自衛。

translations.literal: He greatly exalted himself, wishing to use his commanding fame to hold the distant regions; he built a residence at Shitou and deployed guards and sentries for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated his own prestige, hoping his martial reputation would keep the far provinces in awe. He built a mansion at Shitou and posted guards and patrols around it.

sentences.zh: 尋征拜宗正卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to court and made director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 九年，賜實封一千二百戶。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was granted an income estate of twelve hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he received a taxable fief of twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，遷禮部尚書，以功臣封河間郡王，除觀州刺史，與長孫無忌等代襲刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was transferred to Minister of Rites; as a meritorious official he was enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian Commandery; appointed Prefect of Guanzhou; along with Zhangsun Wuji and others he served as hereditary prefects in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he became minister of rites and, as a founding merit-holder, was enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian. He was named prefect of Guanzhou and, like Zhangsun Wuji and the other great ministers, held that post in the rotating system of nominal prefects.

sentences.zh: 孝恭性奢豪，重遊宴，歌姬舞女百有餘人，然而寬恕退讓，無驕矜自伐之色。

translations.literal: Xiaogong was by nature lavish and proud, fond of feasting and banquets; he had more than a hundred singing girls and dancing women; yet he was forgiving and yielding, without an air of arrogance or self-congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong lived lavishly and loved feasts and entertainments; more than a hundred singers and dancers attended him. Even so, he was generous and unassuming, with none of the swagger of a man who preens on his own achievements.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚加親待，諸宗室中莫與為比。

translations.literal: Taizong treated him with great intimacy and favor; among all members of the imperial clan none could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong favored him with unusual warmth, and no other prince of the clan stood so close to him.

sentences.zh: 孝恭嘗悵然謂所親曰：「吾所居宅微為宏壯，非吾心也，當賣之，別營一所，粗令充事而已。

translations.literal: Xiaogong once said despondently to those close to him: "The residence where I live is somewhat grand and imposing—not what my heart desires. I ought to sell it and build another that is merely adequate for daily needs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong once told his intimates, with a troubled look: "The house I live in has grown a little too grand for my taste. I mean to sell it and build another—something plain, enough only to get by.

sentences.zh: 身歿之後。

translations.literal: After I die,
translations.idiomatic: After I am gone,

sentences.zh: 諸子若才，守此足矣；

translations.literal: if my sons have talent, guarding this will be enough;
translations.idiomatic: if my sons have ability, holding on to that will be enough;

sentences.zh: 如其不才，冀免他人所利也。」

translations.literal: if they lack talent, I hope thereby to spare them from becoming prey for others.
translations.idiomatic: and if they lack ability, I hope at least to keep others from coveting what we have.

sentences.zh: 十四年，暴薨，年五十。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died suddenly, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he died suddenly, at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 太宗素服舉哀，哭之甚慟，贈司空、揚州都督，陪葬獻陵，謚曰元，配享高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: Taizong wore plain mourning garments and held lamentation, weeping for him with great grief; posthumously granted Minister of Works and Area Commander of Yangzhou; buried with attendant honors at Xian Mausoleum; posthumous title Yuan; enshrined in the ancestral temple hall of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong put on plain mourning and grieved for him bitterly. Xiaogong was posthumously made minister of works and area commander of Yangzhou, buried beside Xian Mausoleum with the posthumous name Yuan, and granted a place in the sacrifices at Gaozu's temple.

sentences.zh: 子崇義嗣，降爵為譙國公，歷蒲、同二州刺史，益州大都督長史，甚有威名。

translations.literal: His son Chongyi succeeded; his rank was reduced to Duke of Qiao; he served as Prefect of Pu and Tong prefectures and as Senior Administrator of the Grand Area Commander of Yizhou; he had considerable martial reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongyi succeeded him. His title was lowered to Duke of Qiao. He served as prefect of Pu and Tong and as senior administrator under the grand area commander of Yizhou, and won a strong reputation for authority.

sentences.zh: 後卒於宗正卿。

translations.literal: Later he died while serving as Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while holding the post of director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 孝恭弟瑊，武德中，為尚書右丞，封濟北郡王，卒於始州刺史。

translations.literal: Xiaogong's younger brother Jian, during Wude, served as Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jibei Commandery, and died while Prefect of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong's younger brother Jian served in the Wude era as right assistant director of the masters of writing, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jibei, and died as prefect of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 瑊弟瑰，義師克京城，授瑰左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Gui—when the Righteous Army captured the capital, Gui was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Left.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Gui was made left grand master of splendid happiness when the righteous army took the capital.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，封漢陽郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Duke of Hanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Duke of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his rank was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his title was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為侵寇，高祖使瑰齎布帛數萬段與結和親。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly raided as invaders; Gaozu sent Gui bearing tens of thousands of bolts of cloth and silk to conclude a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were raiding again and again, and Gaozu sent Gui with tens of thousands of bolts of silk and cloth to negotiate a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗初見瑰，箕踞；

translations.literal: When Qaghan Jieli first saw Gui, he sat squatting with legs spread;
translations.idiomatic: When Qaghan Jieli first received Gui, he sat sprawled with legs apart in contempt;

sentences.zh: 瑰餌以厚利，頡利大悅，改容加敬，遣使隨瑰獻名馬。

translations.literal: Gui baited him with great profit; Jieli was greatly pleased, changed his expression to show respect, and sent envoys to follow Gui presenting fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Gui offered lavish gifts. Jieli was delighted, changed his manner, and treated him with respect, then sent envoys back with Gui bearing fine horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 後復將命，頡利謂左右曰：「李瑰前來，恨不屈之，今者必令下拜。」

translations.literal: Later when he again bore the imperial commission, Jieli said to those around him: "When Li Gui came before, I regretted not making him bow; this time I will certainly make him prostrate himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui returned on another mission, Jieli told his attendants: "Last time Li Gui came, I regretted not forcing him to bow. This time I shall make him kowtow.

sentences.zh: 瑰微知之，及見頡利，長揖不屈節。

translations.literal: Gui faintly knew this; when he saw Jieli, he made a deep bow but would not yield in propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had some inkling of the plan. When he met Jieli he gave a deep bow but refused to abase himself.

sentences.zh: 頡利大怒，乃留瑰不遣。

translations.literal: Jieli was greatly angered and detained Gui without releasing him.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli flew into a rage and kept Gui from returning.

sentences.zh: 瑰神意自若，竟不為之屈。

translations.literal: Gui's spirit and bearing remained composed; in the end he would not yield to it.
translations.idiomatic: Gui remained calm and unbroken, and in the end would not submit.

sentences.zh: 頡利知不可以威脅，終禮遣之。

translations.literal: Jieli knew he could not be coerced by intimidation and finally sent him away with proper courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that threats would not move him, Jieli at last sent him home with due ceremony.

sentences.zh: 拜左武候將軍，轉衛尉卿，代兄孝恭為荊州都督。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Left Military Guard; transferred to Chamberlain for the Imperial Stud; replaced his elder brother Xiaogong as Area Commander of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the left military guard, then chamberlain for the imperial stud, and succeeded his elder brother Xiaogong as area commander of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 政存清靜，深為士庶所懷。

translations.literal: His governance aimed at quiet simplicity; he was deeply cherished by gentry and commoners alike.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with restraint and quiet order, and gentry and common people alike held him in deep regard.

sentences.zh: 嶺外豪帥屢相攻擊，遣使喻以威德，皆相次歸附，嶺表遂定。

translations.literal: Outside the Ling region, powerful chieftains repeatedly attacked one another; he sent envoys to instruct them with authority and virtue; all in succession submitted; the regions south of the Ling were thus settled.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Ling passes, local strongmen were constantly at war with one another. Gui sent envoys to win them with a mix of force and grace, and one after another they submitted until the southern frontier was settled.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，例降爵為公。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, by regulation his rank was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, Gui's title was reduced to duke under the usual rule.

sentences.zh: 時長史馮長命曾為御史大夫，素矜衒，事多專決，瑰怒杖之，坐是免。

translations.literal: At that time his senior administrator Feng Changming had once been Censor-in-Chief; he was by nature proud and showy, and on many matters made decisions on his own; Gui angrily had him beaten with sticks; for this Gui was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: His senior administrator Feng Changming, a former censor-in-chief, was vain and overbearing and often decided matters on his own. Gui had him beaten in anger and, for that, was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，拜宜川刺史，加散騎常侍，卒。
