translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was appointed Prefect of Yichuan; added title of Regular Attendant of Dispersed Cavalry; died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was made prefect of Yichuan with the additional title of regular attendant, and there he died.

sentences.zh: 子沖玄，垂拱中官至冬官尚書；

translations.literal: His son Chongxuan, during the Chuigong period reached the office of Minister of Public Works;
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongxuan rose during the Chuigong era to minister of public works;

sentences.zh: 沖虛，卒於尚方監。

translations.literal: Chongxu died while serving as Director of the Imperial Manufactory.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxu died while serving as director of the imperial manufactory.

sentences.zh: 廬江王瑗，高祖從父兄子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Lujiang Yuan was a son of Gaozu's paternal first cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Lujiang Yuan was the son of Gaozu's first cousin once removed.

sentences.zh: 父哲，隋柱國、備身將軍，追封濟南王。

translations.literal: His father Zhe was a Sui Pillar of State and Palace Guard General; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhe had been a Sui pillar of state and palace guard general and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 瑗，武德元年曆信州總管，封廬江王。

translations.literal: Yuan—in the first year of Wude served successively as Overall Commander of Xinzhou and was enfeoffed as Prince of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan served as overall commander of Xinzhou in the first year of Wude and was enfeoffed as Prince of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 九年，累遷幽州大都督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was progressively transferred to Grand Area Commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted step by step to grand area commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以瑗懦曌，非邊將才，遣右領軍將軍王君廓助典兵事。

translations.literal: The court considered Yuan timid and dull, not a talent for a frontier general; it sent Right Rear Guard General Wang Junguo to assist in managing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Yuan too timid and inept for frontier command and sent Right Rear Guard General Wang Junguo to help manage the army.

sentences.zh: 君廓故嘗為盜，勇力絕人，瑗倚仗之，許結婚姻，以布心腹。

translations.literal: Junguo had formerly been a bandit; his courage and strength surpassed others; Yuan relied on him, promised a marriage alliance, to win his confidence as an intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Junguo had once been an outlaw and possessed extraordinary strength and daring. Yuan leaned on him, promised him a marriage tie, and tried to make him a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 時隱太子建成將有異圖，外結於瑗。

translations.literal: At that time the Hidden Heir Jian had designs of irregular ambition and formed external ties with Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the hidden heir Jian was plotting rebellion and cultivated ties with Yuan beyond the capital.

sentences.zh: 及建成誅死，遣通事舍人崔敦禮召瑗入朝，瑗有懼色。

translations.literal: When Jian was executed and killed, they sent Palace Staff Officer Cui Dunli to summon Yuan to court; Yuan showed a look of fear.
translations.idiomatic: After Jian was put to death, the court sent palace staff officer Cui Dunli to summon Yuan to the capital. Yuan's face showed fear.

sentences.zh: 君廓素險薄，欲因事陷之以為己功，遂紿瑗曰：「京都有變，事未可知。

translations.literal: Junguo was by nature treacherous and frivolous; wishing to use the occasion to entrap him for his own merit, he deceived Yuan saying: "There has been a disturbance in the capital; how things stand is not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: Junguo was treacherous by nature and saw a chance to destroy Yuan for his own credit. He lied to him: "There has been trouble in the capital, and no one yet knows how it will end.

sentences.zh: 大王國之懿親，受委作鎮，寧得擁兵數萬而從一使召耶！

translations.literal: Great Prince, you are the state's honored relative, entrusted to hold a frontier command—can you really hold tens of thousands of troops yet obey the summons of a single envoy!
translations.idiomatic: You are the emperor's own kinsman, entrusted with a frontier command—can you keep tens of thousands of soldiers under arms and still obey the call of one lone envoy?

sentences.zh: 且聞趙郡王先以被拘，太子、齊王又言若此，大王今去，能自保乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover I hear the Prince of Zhao was first taken into custody; the Crown Prince and Prince of Qi have spoken as much—if the Great Prince goes now, can you protect yourself?
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Prince of Zhao was seized first, and the crown prince and the Prince of Qi have said as much. If you go now, can you even keep yourself safe?

sentences.zh: 相與共泣。

translations.literal: Together they wept.
translations.idiomatic: The two of them wept together.

sentences.zh: 瑗乃囚敦禮，舉兵反。

translations.literal: Yuan then imprisoned Dunli and raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan then imprisoned Dunli and rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 召北齊州刺史王詵，將與計事，兵曹參軍王利涉說瑗曰：「王不奉詔而擅發兵，此為反矣。

translations.literal: He summoned Prefect of Beiji Wang Shen, intending to consult on plans; Army Aide Wang Lishe urged Yuan: "Your Highness did not receive an edict yet mobilized troops on your own—this is rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Wang Shen, prefect of Beiji, to plan with him. Army aide Wang Lishe urged Yuan: "Your Highness has mobilized troops without imperial orders. That is rebellion.

sentences.zh: 須改易法度，以權宜應變，先定眾心。

translations.literal: You must change laws and institutions, adapt flexibly to circumstances, and first settle the hearts of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: You must change the rules of command, act as circumstances require, and first secure the loyalty of the men.

sentences.zh: 今諸州刺史或有逆命，王徵兵不集，何以保全？」

translations.literal: Now if some prefects should disobey and Your Highness cannot assemble troops when you levy them—how will you preserve yourself?
translations.idiomatic: If some prefects refuse your orders and your levies fail to gather, how will you protect yourself?

sentences.zh: 瑗曰：「若之何？」

translations.literal: Yuan said: "What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan asked: "What should I do?"

sentences.zh: 利涉曰：「山東之地，先從竇建德，酋豪首領，皆是偽官，今並黜之，退居匹庶，此人思亂，若旱苗之望雨。

translations.literal: Lishe said: "In the Shandong region, those who formerly followed Dou Jiande—chieftains and leaders—all held positions under the rebel regime; now they have all been dismissed and sent down to commoner status; these men long for turmoil like drought-stricken seedlings longing for rain.
translations.idiomatic: Lishe said: "In the Shandong region, the chieftains who once served Dou Jiande were all given posts under the rebel regime. They have since been stripped of office and reduced to commoners. Those men hunger for chaos the way drought-stricken fields hunger for rain.

sentences.zh: 王宜發使復其舊職，各於所在遣募本兵，諸州倘有不從，即委隨便誅戮。

translations.literal: Your Highness should send envoys to restore them to their former posts, have each recruit their original troops locally; if any prefecture should not obey, authorize them to execute as they see fit.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness should send envoys to restore them to their old posts and let each raise his former followers where he stands. If any prefecture refuses, authorize them to kill as they see fit.

sentences.zh: 此計若行，河北之地可呼吸而定也。

translations.literal: If this plan is carried out, the Hebei region can be settled in the time of a breath.
translations.idiomatic: If that plan succeeds, all of Hebei can be taken almost at a breath.

sentences.zh: 然後分遣王詵北連突厥，道自太原，南臨蒲、絳；

translations.literal: Then dispatch Wang Shen north to ally with the Turks, his route from Taiyuan south pressing on Pu and Jiang;
translations.idiomatic: Then send Wang Shen north to join with the Turks, marching from Taiyuan south toward Pu and Jiang;

sentences.zh: 大王整駕親詣洛陽，西入潼關。

translations.literal: Your Highness should array your carriage and personally proceed to Luoyang, entering Tong Pass from the west.
translations.idiomatic: while Your Highness yourself leads the main force to Luoyang and enters Tong Pass from the west.

sentences.zh: 兩軍合勢，不盈旬月，天下定矣。」

translations.literal: The two armies joining strength—in less than a ten-day month the realm will be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Once the two armies unite, the realm will be settled in less than a month."

sentences.zh: 瑗從之。

translations.literal: Yuan followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 瑗以內外機悉付君廓。

translations.literal: Yuan entrusted all internal and external affairs entirely to Junguo.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan put every civil and military matter entirely in Junguo's hands.

sentences.zh: 利涉以君廓多翻覆，又說瑗委兵於王詵而除君廓，瑗不能決。

translations.literal: Lishe, because Junguo was much given to turning and overturning, again urged Yuan to entrust the army to Wang Shen and remove Junguo; Yuan could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Lishe, distrusting Junguo's fickleness, urged Yuan to give the army to Wang Shen and remove Junguo. Yuan could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 君廓知之，馳斬詵，持首告其眾曰：「李瑗與王詵共反，禁錮敕使，擅追兵集。

translations.literal: Junguo learned of this, galloped to kill Shen, and holding up the head told the troops: "Li Yuan and Wang Shen rebelled together, imprisoned the imperial envoy, and on their own authority raised and assembled troops.
translations.idiomatic: Junguo learned of it, rode out, and killed Shen. Holding up the head, he told the troops: "Li Yuan and Wang Shen have rebelled together. They imprisoned the imperial envoy and raised troops on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 今王詵已斬，獨李瑗在，無能為也。

translations.literal: Now Wang Shen has been beheaded; only Li Yuan remains—he can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen is already dead. Only Li Yuan remains, and he can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 汝若從之，終亦族滅；

translations.literal: If you follow him, in the end your entire clans will be exterminated;
translations.idiomatic: If you follow him, your whole clans will be wiped out in the end;

sentences.zh: 從我取之，立得富貴。

translations.literal: follow me and seize him, and you will immediately gain wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: follow me and seize him, and wealth and rank are yours at once.

sentences.zh: 禍福如是，意欲何從？」

translations.literal: Fortune and disaster stand thus—what do you intend to follow?
translations.idiomatic: Disaster or reward lies before you— which will you choose?

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「皆願討賊。」

translations.literal: The troops said: "We all wish to strike down the rebel."
translations.idiomatic: The men answered: "We all wish to strike down the rebel."

sentences.zh: 君廓領其麾下登城西面，瑗未之覺。

translations.literal: Junguo led his subordinates onto the west side of the city wall; Yuan did not yet know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Junguo led his men onto the west wall of the city. Yuan knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 君廓自領千餘人先往獄中出敦禮，瑗始知之，遽率數百人披甲，才出至門外，與君廓相遇。

translations.literal: Junguo himself led more than a thousand men first to the prison to release Dunli; Yuan only then learned of it; he hastily led several hundred men in armor; just as he emerged outside the gate he met Junguo.
translations.idiomatic: Junguo himself took more than a thousand men to the prison and freed Dunli. Only then did Yuan learn what was happening. He rushed out with several hundred armored men, and just beyond the gate he ran into Junguo.

sentences.zh: 君廓謂其眾曰：「李瑗作逆誤人，何忽從之，自取塗炭？」

translations.literal: Junguo said to his troops: "Li Yuan has rebelled and misled people—why did you suddenly follow him and bring ruin on yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: Junguo shouted to the men: "Li Yuan has led you into rebellion—why follow him to your own destruction?

sentences.zh: 眾皆倒戈，一時潰走。

translations.literal: All turned their weapons against him; in an instant they broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They turned their weapons at once and broke in flight.

sentences.zh: 瑗塊然獨存，謂君廓曰：「小人賣我以自媚，汝行當自及矣。」

translations.literal: Yuan stood alone and isolated, and said to Junguo: "A petty man sold me out to curry favor—you in turn will soon meet the same fate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan stood utterly alone and said to Junguo: "A villain sold me out to win favor. The same fate will come for you soon enough.

sentences.zh: 君廓擒瑗，縊殺之，年四十一，傳首京師，絕其屬籍。

translations.literal: Junguo seized Yuan, strangled him to death; he was forty-one; his head was sent to the capital; his clan register was annulled.
translations.idiomatic: Junguo seized Yuan and strangled him. Yuan was forty-one. His head was sent to the capital, and his name was struck from the imperial clan rolls.

sentences.zh: 君廓，并州石艾人也。

translations.literal: Junguo was a native of Shiai in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Junguo was a native of Shiai in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少亡命為群盜，聚徒千餘人，轉掠長平，進逼夏縣。

translations.literal: In youth he became an outlaw and led a band of bandits; gathering more than a thousand followers, he roved and plundered Changping, pressing forward against Xia County.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he became an outlaw and gathered more than a thousand followers. He raided across Changping and pressed toward Xia County.

sentences.zh: 李密遣使召之，遂投於密。

translations.literal: Li Mi sent envoys to summon him; he thereupon joined Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi sent envoys to summon him, and he went over to Mi's side.

sentences.zh: 尋又率眾歸國，歷遷右武衛將軍，累封彭國公。

translations.literal: Before long he again led his followers to submit to the dynasty; he was progressively promoted to General of the Right Military Guard; was repeatedly enfeoffed up to Duke of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led his men back to Tang service, rose to general of the right military guard, and was enfeoffed in stages up to Duke of Peng.

sentences.zh: 從平劉黑闥，令鎮幽州。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Liu Heita and was ordered to garrison Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Liu Heita and was ordered to hold Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 會突厥入寇，君廓邀擊破之，俘斬二千餘人，獲馬五千匹。

translations.literal: When the Turks invaded, Junguo intercepted and defeated them, capturing and killing more than two thousand, seizing five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks invaded, Junguo intercepted them, routed their force, killed or captured more than two thousand men, and took five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，徵入朝，賜以御馬，令於殿庭乘之而出，因謂侍臣曰：「吾聞藺相如叱秦皇，目皆出血。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased, summoned him to court, bestowed an imperial horse, had him mount it in the palace courtyard and ride out, and then said to attending ministers: "I have heard that when Lin Xiangru berated the Qin Emperor, blood flowed from his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted, summoned him to court, and gave him an imperial horse. He had Junguo mount it in the palace courtyard and ride out, then told the ministers: "I have heard that when Lin Xiangru rebuked the First Emperor of Qin, blood burst from his eyes.

sentences.zh: 君廓往擊竇建德，將出戰，李靖遏之，君廓發憤大呼，目及鼻耳一時流血。

translations.literal: When Junguo went to strike Dou Jiande, about to enter battle, Li Jing held him back; Junguo in furious indignation cried out, and blood flowed simultaneously from his eyes, nose, and ears.
translations.idiomatic: When Junguo went to fight Dou Jiande and was about to charge, Li Jing held him back. Junguo roared in fury, and blood streamed from his eyes, nose, and ears at once.

sentences.zh: 此之壯氣，何謝古人，不可以常例賞之。」

translations.literal: Such fierce spirit—what need to defer to the ancients! He cannot be rewarded by ordinary precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit like that need not yield to the ancients. Such a man cannot be rewarded by ordinary measure.

sentences.zh: 復賜錦袍金帶，還鎮幽州。

translations.literal: He was again granted a brocade robe and gold belt and returned to garrison Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a brocade robe and gold belt and sent back to hold Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以誅瑗功，拜左領軍大將軍，兼幽州都督，以瑗家口賜之，加左光祿大夫，賜物千段，食實封千三百戶。

translations.literal: Soon for the merit of killing Yuan he was appointed Great General of the Left Rear Guard, concurrently Area Commander of Youzhou; Yuan's household was given to him; added title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Left; granted a thousand bolts of goods; income estate of thirteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for killing Yuan, he was made great general of the left rear guard and area commander of Youzhou. Yuan's household was given to him, along with the title of left grand master of splendid happiness, a thousand bolts of goods, and a fief of thirteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 在職多縱逸，長史李玄道數以朝憲脅之，懼為所奏，殊不自安。

translations.literal: In office he was much given to lax indulgence; Senior Administrator Li Xuandao repeatedly threatened him with court law; fearing being reported by him, he was very ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In office he indulged himself freely. His senior administrator Li Xuandao often warned him with threats of impeachment under court law. Junguo feared a report against him and grew deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 後追入朝，行至渭南，殺驛史而遁。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to court; when he reached Weinan he killed the post-station clerk and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When he was later summoned to court, he reached Weinan, killed the post-station clerk, and fled.

sentences.zh: 將奔突厥，為野人所殺，追削其封邑。

translations.literal: As he was about to flee to the Turks he was killed by country people; his enfeoffment was posthumously revoked.
translations.idiomatic: He was making for the Turks when country people killed him. His fief was afterward revoked.

sentences.zh: 淮陽王道玄，高祖從父兄子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Huaiyang Daoxuan was a son of Gaozu's paternal first cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huaiyang Daoxuan was the son of Gaozu's first cousin once removed.

sentences.zh: 祖繪，隋夏州總管，武德初，追封雍王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was Sui Overall Commander of Xiazhou; at the beginning of Wude posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui had been Sui overall commander of Xiazhou and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yong at the start of Wude.

sentences.zh: 父贄，追封河南王。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 道玄，武德元年封淮陽王，授右千牛。

translations.literal: Daoxuan—in the first year of Wude enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyang, appointed Right Thousand-Ox Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyang in the first year of Wude and appointed right thousand-ox attendant.

sentences.zh: 從太宗擊宋金剛於介州，先登陷陣，時年十五，太宗壯之，賞物千段。

translations.literal: Following Taizong he attacked Song Jingang at Jiezhou, first to scale the walls and break the formation; he was then fifteen; Taizong admired his feat and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong against Song Jingang at Jiezhou, was first over the wall and into the enemy line. He was fifteen at the time. Taizong admired his courage and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 後從討王世充，頻戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Later he followed in the campaign against Wang Shichong; in repeated battles he was always victorious.
translations.idiomatic: He later campaigned against Wang Shichong and won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 竇建德至武牢，太宗以輕騎誘賊，領道玄率伏兵於道左，會賊至，追擊破之。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande reached Wulao, Taizong used light cavalry to lure the enemy; leading Daoxuan he stationed hidden troops on the left of the road; when the enemy arrived they pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande reached Wulao, Taizong baited the enemy with light cavalry. Daoxuan led hidden troops on the left of the road, and when the enemy came up they pursued and broke them.

sentences.zh: 又從太宗轉戰於汜水，麾戈陷陣，直出賊後，眾披靡，復衝突而歸。

translations.literal: Again following Taizong he fought at Sishui; brandishing his halberd he broke the formation, drove straight behind the enemy lines; the masses scattered; then he charged back through and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Sishui he fought again under Taizong. Waving his halberd he smashed through the enemy line, drove deep behind their rear, sent the ranks scattering, and then cut his way back out.

sentences.zh: 太宗大悅，命副乘以給道玄。

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly pleased and ordered spare chariots given to Daoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was delighted and ordered spare chariots assigned to Daoxuan.

sentences.zh: 又從太宗赴賊，再入再出，飛矢亂下，箭如蝟毛，猛氣益厲，射人無不應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Again following Taizong he rode toward the enemy; twice in and twice out; flying arrows rained down chaotically, arrows thick as a hedgehog's bristles; his fierce spirit grew only fiercer; every man he shot fell at the twang of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: He rode with Taizong straight at the enemy again, plunging in and out twice while arrows fell like rain and clustered thick as a hedgehog's quills. His fighting fury only mounted, and every man he shot dropped the moment the bowstring sang.

sentences.zh: 東都平，拜洛州總管。

translations.literal: When the eastern capital was pacified, he was appointed Overall Commander of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern capital was pacified, he was appointed overall commander of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 及府廢，改授洛州刺史。

translations.literal: When the commandery was abolished, he was reassigned as Prefect of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When that commandery was abolished, he was reassigned as prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，劉黑闥引突厥寇河北，復授山東道行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Liu Heita led the Turks to raid Hebei; he was again appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Shandong Circuit campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wude, Liu Heita led Turkic forces to raid Hebei, and Daoxuan was again appointed commander-in-chief of the Shandong circuit campaign army.

sentences.zh: 師次下博，與賊軍遇，道玄帥騎先登，命副將史萬寶督軍繼進。

translations.literal: The army halted at Xiabo and encountered the rebel force; Daoxuan led the cavalry forward first and ordered his deputy Shi Wanbao to supervise the army following behind.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Xiabo and met the rebel host. Daoxuan led the cavalry in the first charge and ordered his deputy, Shi Wanbao, to bring the main body up behind him.

sentences.zh: 萬寶與之不協，及道玄深入，而擁兵不進，謂所親曰：「吾奉手詔，言淮陽小兒雖名為將，而軍之進止皆委於吾。

translations.literal: Wanbao was at odds with him; when Daoxuan pressed deep in, Wanbao held his troops and did not advance, saying to his intimates: "I received a handwritten edict saying that though the Huaiyang boy bears the name of general, all advance and withdrawal of the army is entrusted to me.
translations.idiomatic: Wanbao was at odds with him. When Daoxuan drove deep into enemy territory, Wanbao held his troops back and would not advance. He told his confidants, "I received a handwritten edict saying that although the boy of Huaiyang bears the title of general, all movement of the army is entrusted to me.

sentences.zh: 今其輕脫，越濘交戰，大軍若動，必陷泥溺，莫如結陣以待之，雖不利於王，而利於國。」

translations.literal: Now he is rash and reckless, crossing the marsh to give battle; if the main army moves, it will surely sink in mud and mire; better to form ranks and wait—though unfavorable to the prince, it favors the state.
translations.idiomatic: Now he is rash: he is crossing the marsh to give battle. If the main army moves, it will surely bog down in mud and mire. Better to hold formation and wait. It may go ill for the prince, but it will serve the state.

sentences.zh: 道玄遂為賊所擒，全軍盡沒，惟萬寶逃歸。

translations.literal: Daoxuan was thereupon captured by the rebels; the whole army was destroyed; only Wanbao escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan was captured by the enemy, the entire army was wiped out, and only Wanbao escaped and made it back.

sentences.zh: 道玄遇害，年十九。

translations.literal: Daoxuan met a violent death; he was nineteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan was killed in battle. He was nineteen.

sentences.zh: 太宗追悼久之，嘗從容謂侍臣曰：「道玄終始從朕，見朕深入賊陣，所向必克，意嘗企慕，所以每陣先登，蓋學朕也。

translations.literal: Taizong mourned him at length; once, in relaxed conversation, he told his attendants: "Daoxuan followed me from start to finish; seeing me plunge deep into enemy formations and prevail wherever I turned, he admired me in his heart; that is why at every battle he led the charge first—he was imitating me.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned him for a long while. Once, speaking at ease to his attendants, he said, "Daoxuan followed me from beginning to end. He saw me plunge deep into enemy lines and prevail wherever I turned, and he admired that in his heart. That is why at every battle he charged first—he was trying to be like me.

sentences.zh: 惜其年少，不遂遠圖。」

translations.literal: Pity that he was so young and could not fulfill his greater ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: It is a pity he was so young and never had the chance to realize his greater ambitions.

sentences.zh: 因為之流涕。

translations.literal: As he spoke he wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: As he spoke, he wept for Daoxuan.

sentences.zh: 贈左驍衛大將軍，謚曰壯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the post of Left Brave Cavalry Grand General, with the posthumous designation Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand general of the Left Brave Cavalry Guard, with the posthumous name Zhuang ["Valiant"].

sentences.zh: 無子，詔封其弟武都郡公道明為淮陽王，令主道玄之祀。

translations.literal: Having no son, an edict enfeoffed his younger brother, Commander of Wudong Commandery Daoming, as Prince of Huaiyang and charged him with maintaining Daoxuan's sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan had no son. An edict enfeoffed his younger brother Daoming, commander of Wudong commandery, as Prince of Huaiyang and charged him with maintaining Daoxuan's ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 累遷左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to General of the Left Brave Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming was promoted in stages to general of the Left Brave Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 送弘化公主還蕃，坐洩主非太宗女，奪爵國除，後卒於鄆州刺史。

translations.literal: While escorting Princess Honghua back to the frontier tribes, he was convicted of revealing that the princess was not Taizong's daughter; his title was revoked and his fief abolished; later he died while serving as Prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting Princess Honghua back to the tribes, he was convicted of revealing that the princess was not Taizong's daughter. His title was revoked and his fief abolished. He later died while serving as prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 江夏王道宗，道玄從父弟也。

translations.literal: Prince Jiangxia Daozong was Daoxuan's younger paternal first cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiangxia Daozong was Daoxuan's younger paternal first cousin.

sentences.zh: 父韶，追封東平王，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Shao was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping and given the posthumous gift title Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping and given the posthumous title of minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 道宗，武德元年封略陽郡公，起家左千牛備身。

translations.literal: Daozong—in the first year of Wude was enfeoffed as Duke of Lueyang Commandery and began his career as Left Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong was enfeoffed as duke of Lueyang commandery in the first year of Wude and began his career as a left thousand-ox guard attendant.

sentences.zh: 討劉武周，戰於度索原，軍敗，賊徒進逼河東。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Liu Wuzhou, they fought at Dusuo Plain; the army was defeated and the rebel host pressed toward Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Liu Wuzhou, they fought at Dusuo Plain. The army was defeated, and the rebel host pressed toward Hedong.

sentences.zh: 道宗時年十七，從太宗率眾拒之。

translations.literal: Daozong was then seventeen and followed Taizong in leading troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong was seventeen at the time. He followed Taizong in leading troops to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 太宗登玉壁城望賊，顧謂道宗曰：「賊恃其眾來邀我戰，汝謂如何？」

translations.literal: Taizong climbed Yubi City to look out at the enemy and, turning to Daozong, said: "The enemy relies on their numbers to challenge us to battle—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong climbed Yubi City to look out at the enemy, then turned to Daozong and said, "The rebels are counting on their numbers to challenge us to battle. What do you think we should do?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「群賊乘勝，其鋒不可當，易以計屈，難與力競。

translations.literal: He replied: "These bandits ride their victory—their edge cannot be met head-on; they are easy to overcome by stratagem and hard to match in brute force.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "These bandits are riding a victory—their momentum cannot be met head-on. They are easier to break by stratagem than to overpower by force.

sentences.zh: 今深壁高壘，以挫其鋒；

translations.literal: Now we should fortify our walls and raise high ramparts to blunt their edge.
translations.idiomatic: We should now strengthen our walls and raise high ramparts to blunt their momentum.

sentences.zh: 烏合之徒，莫能持久，糧運致竭，自當離散，可不戰而擒。」

translations.literal: This rabble cannot endure long; when their grain supply is exhausted they will scatter of themselves, and we can take them without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: This is a mob that cannot hold together for long. Once their grain runs out, they will scatter on their own, and we can take them without fighting."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「汝意暗與我合。」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Your view secretly agrees with mine."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Your thinking quietly matches my own."

sentences.zh: 後賊果食盡夜遁，追及介州，一戰滅之。

translations.literal: Later the enemy indeed ran out of food and fled by night; pursued to Jiezhou, they were destroyed in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later the enemy did run out of food and fled by night. Pursued to Jiezhou, they were wiped out in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 又從平竇建德，破王世充，屢有殊效。

translations.literal: He also followed in the pacification of Dou Jiande and the defeat of Wang Shichong, repeatedly achieving exceptional results.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in pacifying Dou Jiande and defeating Wang Shichong, winning repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 五年，授靈州總管。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Overall Commander of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wude he was appointed overall commander of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁師都據夏州，遣弟洛仁引突厥兵數萬至於城下。

translations.literal: Liang Shidu held Xiazhou and sent his younger brother Luoren to lead tens of thousands of Turkic troops to the foot of the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shidu held Xiazhou and sent his younger brother Luoren to lead tens of thousands of Turkic troops to the foot of the city walls.

sentences.zh: 道宗閉門拒守，伺隙而戰，賊徒大敗。

translations.literal: Daozong shut the gates and held firm, then struck when he found an opening; the rebel host suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong shut the gates and held firm, then struck when he saw an opening. The rebel host was routed.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘉之，謂左僕射裴寂、中書令蕭瑀曰：「道宗今能守邊，以寡制眾。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard and praised him; he told Left Vice Director Pei Ji and Director of the Secretariat Xiao Yu: "Daozong can now defend the frontier, using the few to control the many.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard of it and praised him. He told left vice director Pei Ji and director of the secretariat Xiao Yu, "Daozong can now defend the frontier and use the few to control the many.

sentences.zh: 昔魏任城王彰臨戎卻敵，道宗勇敢，有同於彼。」

translations.literal: In antiquity Wei Prince of Rencheng Zhang faced the army and repelled the enemy; Daozong's bravery is like his.
translations.idiomatic: In olden times Wei Prince of Rencheng Zhang faced the enemy in battle and drove them back. Daozong's courage is the same.

sentences.zh: 遂封為任城王。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was enfeoffed as Prince of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was enfeoffed as Prince of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥連於梁師都，其郁射設入居五原舊地，道宗逐出之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Turks had allied with Liang Shidu; their Yusheshe leader had entered and occupied the old lands of Wuyuan—Daozong drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Turks had allied with Liang Shidu, and their Yusheshe leader had entered and occupied the old territory of Wuyuan. Daozong drove him out.

sentences.zh: 振耀威武，開拓疆界，斥地千餘里，邊人悅服。

translations.literal: He displayed martial prestige, expanded the frontier, and pushed the border outward more than a thousand li; border peoples submitted with approval.
translations.idiomatic: He displayed martial prestige, expanded the frontier, and pushed the border outward more than a thousand li. The peoples of the border submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，征拜鴻臚卿，歷左領軍、大理卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies, then served successively as Left Central Guard Commander and Grand Judge of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed grand master of ceremonies, then served successively as left central guard commander and grand judge of Dali.

sentences.zh: 時太宗將經略突厥，又拜靈州都督。

translations.literal: As Taizong was about to launch operations against the Turks, he was again appointed Area Commander of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Taizong was preparing operations against the Turks, Daozong was again appointed area commander of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，為大同道行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the third year he became Commander-in-Chief of the Datong Circuit campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan he became commander-in-chief of the Datong circuit campaign army.

sentences.zh: 遇李靖襲破頡利可汗，頡利以十餘騎來奔其部。

translations.literal: He encountered the situation where Li Jing had struck and shattered Khan Jieli; Jieli came fleeing to Daozong's command with a little over ten riders.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Jing had struck and shattered Khan Jieli, and Jieli fled to Daozong's command with a little more than ten riders.

sentences.zh: 道宗引兵逼之，征其執送頡利。

translations.literal: Daozong led troops to press him and demanded that Jieli be seized and delivered up.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong led troops to press him and demanded that Jieli be seized and sent in.

sentences.zh: 頡利以數騎夜走，匿於荒谷，沙鈐羅懼，馳追獲之，遣使送於京師。

translations.literal: Jieli fled by night with a few riders and hid in a desolate valley; Shachaluo, in fear, galloped in pursuit and captured him, then sent envoys to deliver him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli fled by night with a few riders and hid in a desolate valley. Shachaluo, in fear, galloped after him, captured him, and sent envoys to deliver him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以功賜實封六百戶，召拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: For this merit he was granted six hundred households of substantive fief income and summoned to serve as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was granted six hundred households of substantive fief income and summoned to serve as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾寇邊，詔右僕射李靖為昆丘道行軍大總管，道宗與吏部尚書侯君集為之副。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun raided the border, an edict appointed Right Vice Director Li Jing supreme commander of the Kunqiu Circuit campaign army, with Daozong and Minister of Civil Appointments Hou Junji as his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raided the border, an edict appointed right vice director Li Jing supreme commander of the Kunqiu circuit campaign army, with Daozong and minister of civil appointments Hou Junji as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 賊聞兵至，走入嶂山，已行數千里。

translations.literal: Hearing the army had arrived, the enemy fled into the Zhang Mountains, already having marched several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy heard the army had arrived, they fled into the Zhang Mountains, already having marched several thousand li.

sentences.zh: 諸將議欲息兵，道宗固請追討，李靖然之，而君集不從。

translations.literal: The generals discussed halting the campaign; Daozong firmly petitioned to pursue and destroy them; Li Jing agreed, but Junji did not.
translations.idiomatic: The generals discussed halting the campaign, but Daozong firmly petitioned to pursue and destroy the enemy. Li Jing agreed; Junji did not.

sentences.zh: 道宗遂率偏師並行倍道，去大軍十日，追及之。

translations.literal: Daozong thereupon led a detached column on a parallel forced march, ten days ahead of the main army, and overtook the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong then led a detached column on a parallel forced march, ten days ahead of the main army, and overtook the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊據險苦戰，道宗潛遣千餘騎逾山襲其後，賊表裡受敵，一時奔潰。

translations.literal: The enemy held the high ground and fought bitterly; Daozong secretly sent more than a thousand cavalry over the mountains to strike their rear; caught between attacks from front and rear, they broke and fled all at once.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy held the high ground and fought bitterly. Daozong secretly sent more than a thousand cavalry over the mountains to strike their rear. Caught between attacks from front and back, they broke and fled at once.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷禮部尚書，改封江夏王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Minister of Rites and his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhenguan he was transferred to minister of rites and his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 尋坐贓下獄。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was imprisoned on charges of embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was imprisoned on charges of embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂侍臣曰：「朕富有四海，士馬如林，欲使轍跡周宇內，遊觀無休息，絕域采奇玩，海外訪珍羞，豈不得耶？

translations.literal: Taizong said to his attendants: "I possess all within the four seas, with soldiers and horses thick as a forest; if I wished to leave wheel tracks across the whole realm, tour without cease, gather curious treasures from distant lands, and seek rare delicacies from beyond the seas—could I not do so?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said to his attendants, "I possess all within the four seas, with soldiers and horses thick as a forest. If I wished to leave wheel tracks across the whole realm, tour without cease, gather curious treasures from distant lands, and seek rare delicacies from beyond the seas—could I not do so?

sentences.zh: 勞萬姓而樂一人，朕所不取也。

translations.literal: To weary the myriad people for one man's pleasure—that is what I will not accept.
translations.idiomatic: To wear out the myriad people for one man's pleasure—that is what I will not accept.

sentences.zh: 人心無厭，唯當以理制之。

translations.literal: Human desire knows no satiety; one must only restrain it through reason.
translations.idiomatic: The human heart knows no limit to desire. One must restrain it through reason alone.

sentences.zh: 道宗俸料甚高，宴賜不少，足有餘財，而貪婪如此，使人嗟惋，豈不鄙乎！」

translations.literal: Daozong's salary is very high, his banquet gifts no small sum—he has ample surplus wealth; yet he is so greedy as this. It makes one sigh with regret. Is it not contemptible!
translations.idiomatic: Daozong's salary is very high and his banquet gifts no small matter. He has more than enough wealth, yet he is this greedy. It makes one sigh with regret. Is that not contemptible?

sentences.zh: 遂免官，削封邑。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was dismissed from office and his fief income was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was dismissed from office and his fief income was cut.

sentences.zh: 十三年，起為茂州都督，未行，轉晉州刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was restored as Area Commander of Maozhou; before he could depart he was transferred to Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was restored as area commander of Maozhou, but before he could take up the post he was transferred to prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，復拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was again appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was again appointed minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時侯君集立功於高昌，自負其才，潛有異志。

translations.literal: At this time Hou Junji had won merit in Gaochang; proud of his talent, he secretly harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Hou Junji had won distinction in Gaochang. Proud of his talent, he secretly harbored rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 道宗嘗因侍宴，從容言曰：「君集智小言大，舉止不倫，以臣觀之，必為戎首。」

translations.literal: Once, while attending a banquet, Daozong said at ease: "Junji has little wisdom but talks big; his conduct is irregular. In my view he will surely become the ringleader of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending a banquet, Daozong said at ease, "Junji has little wisdom but talks big, and his conduct is irregular. In my view he will surely become the ringleader of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「何以知之？」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "How do you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "How do you know this?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「見其恃有微功，深懷矜伐，恥在房玄齡、李靖之下。

translations.literal: He replied: "I see him rely on his slight merit and deeply cherish boasting; he is ashamed to rank below Fang Xuanling and Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I see him rely on his slight merit and deeply cherish boasting. He is ashamed to rank below Fang Xuanling and Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 雖為吏部尚書，未滿其志，非毀時賢，常有不平之語。」

translations.literal: Though he is Minister of Civil Appointments, this does not satisfy his ambition; he slanders the worthy men of the age and often speaks words of resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Though he is minister of civil appointments, that does not satisfy his ambition. He slanders the worthy men of the age and often speaks words of resentment."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「不可億度，浪生猜貳。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "One must not guess rashly and idly breed suspicion and division.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "One must not guess rashly and idly breed suspicion and division.

sentences.zh: 其功勳才用，無所不堪，朕豈惜重位？

translations.literal: His achievements and talents can fill any role—would I begrudge him a weighty post?
translations.idiomatic: His achievements and talents can fill any role. Would I begrudge him a weighty post?

sentences.zh: 第未到耳。」

translations.literal: It has simply not yet come to that."
translations.idiomatic: It has simply not yet come to that."

sentences.zh: 俄而君集謀反誅，太宗笑謂道宗曰：「君集之事，果如公所揣。」

translations.literal: Before long Junji plotted rebellion and was executed; Taizong smiled and said to Daozong: "Junji's affair unfolded exactly as you foresaw."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Junji plotted rebellion and was executed. Taizong smiled and said to Daozong, "Junji's affair unfolded exactly as you foresaw."

sentences.zh: 及大軍討高麗，令道宗與李靖為前鋒，濟遼水，克蓋牟城。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned against Goryeo, he ordered Daozong and Li Jing to serve as vanguard; they crossed the Liao River and captured Gaimou City.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army campaigned against Goryeo, he ordered Daozong and Li Jing to serve as vanguard. They crossed the Liao River and captured Gaimou City.

sentences.zh: 逢賊兵大至，軍中僉欲深溝保險，待太宗至徐進，道宗曰：「不可。

translations.literal: When enemy troops arrived in great numbers, everyone in the army wanted to dig deep trenches and hold the defensible ground, waiting for Taizong to arrive before advancing slowly; Daozong said: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy troops arrived in great numbers, everyone in the army wanted to dig deep trenches, hold the defensible ground, and wait for Taizong to arrive before advancing slowly. Daozong said, "That will not do.

sentences.zh: 賊赴急遠來，兵實疲頓，恃眾輕我，一戰必摧。

translations.literal: The enemy came from afar in haste; their troops are truly exhausted; relying on their numbers they look down on us—with one battle they can surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy came from afar in haste. Their troops are truly exhausted. Relying on their numbers, they look down on us. One battle will surely break them.

sentences.zh: 昔耿弇不以賊遺君父，我既職在前軍，當須清道以待輿駕。」

translations.literal: In antiquity Geng Yan would not leave the enemy for his sovereign and father; since I hold the duty of the vanguard, I must clear the road and await the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In olden times Geng Yan would not leave the enemy for his sovereign and father. Since I hold the duty of the vanguard, I must clear the road and await the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 李靖然之。

translations.literal: Li Jing agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃與壯士數十騎直衝賊陣，左右出入，靖因合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Then with several dozen picked horsemen he charged straight into the enemy formation, wheeling in and out to left and right; Jing thereupon joined the attack and they inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Then, with several dozen picked horsemen, he charged straight into the enemy formation, wheeling in and out to left and right. Jing joined the attack, and they inflicted a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 太宗至，深加賞勞，賜奴婢四十人。

translations.literal: When Taizong arrived he rewarded him handsomely and granted him forty slaves.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong arrived, he rewarded Daozong handsomely and granted him forty slaves.

sentences.zh: 又築土山攻安市城，土山崩，道宗失於部署，為賊所據。

translations.literal: They also built an earthen mound to assault Ansi City; the mound collapsed; Daozong had been negligent in his deployment, and the enemy seized it.
translations.idiomatic: They also built an earthen mound to assault Ansi City. The mound collapsed. Daozong had been negligent in his deployment, and the enemy seized it.

sentences.zh: 歸罪於果毅傅伏愛，斬之。

translations.literal: He placed the blame on Guoyi officer Fu Fu'ai and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: He placed the blame on guoyi officer Fu Fu'ai and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 道宗跣行詣旗下請罪，太宗曰：「漢武殺王恢，不如秦穆赦孟明，土山之失，且非其罪。」

translations.literal: Daozong went barefoot to the command banner to plead guilty; Taizong said: "Emperor Wu of Han killing Wang Hui was not as good as Duke Mu of Qin pardoning Meng Ming; the loss of the earthen mound was not truly his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong went barefoot to the command banner to plead guilty. Taizong said, "When Emperor Wu of Han killed Wang Hui, that was not as good as when Duke Mu of Qin pardoned Meng Ming. The loss of the earthen mound was not truly his fault.

sentences.zh: 舍而不問。

translations.literal: He released the matter and did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: He released the matter and did not pursue it.

sentences.zh: 道宗在陣損足，太宗親為其針，賜以御膳。

translations.literal: Daozong was wounded in the foot during battle; Taizong personally stitched the wound for him and granted him food from the imperial table.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong was wounded in the foot during battle. Taizong personally stitched the wound for him and granted him food from the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以疾請居閒職，轉太常卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, citing illness, he requested a less demanding post and was transferred to Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan, citing illness, he requested a less demanding post and was transferred to chamberlain for ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，加授特進，增實封並前六百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui he was additionally granted the honorary rank Tejin, and his substantive fief income was increased to six hundred households in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonghui he was additionally granted the honorary rank tejin, and his substantive fief income was increased to six hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 四年，房遺愛伏誅，長孫無忌、褚遂良素與道宗不協，上言道宗與遺愛交結，配流象州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Fang Yi'ai was executed; Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang, who had long been at odds with Daozong, reported that Daozong had associated with Yi'ai; he was sentenced to exile in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yonghui, Fang Yi'ai was executed. Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang, who had long been at odds with Daozong, reported that Daozong had associated with Yi'ai. He was sentenced to exile in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 道病卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: He died of illness on the road; he was fifty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness on the road. He was fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 及無忌、遂良得罪，詔復其官爵。

translations.literal: When Wuji and Suiliang themselves fell from favor, an edict restored Daozong's offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuji and Suiliang themselves fell from favor, an edict restored Daozong's offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 道宗晚年頗好學，敬慕賢士，不以地勢凌人，宗室中唯道宗及河間王孝恭昆季最為當代所重。

translations.literal: In his later years Daozong greatly devoted himself to learning, revered worthy men, and did not lord his rank over others; among the imperial clan, only Daozong and the brothers Prince of Hejian Xiaogong were most highly esteemed in their generation.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Daozong greatly devoted himself to learning, revered worthy men, and did not lord his rank over others. Among the imperial clan, only Daozong and the brothers Prince of Hejian Xiaogong were most highly esteemed in their generation.

sentences.zh: 道宗子景恆，降封盧國公，官至相州刺史。

translations.literal: Daozong's son Jingheng was demoted in rank to Duke of Lu and reached the office of Prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong's son Jingheng was demoted in rank to duke of Lu and reached the office of prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 隴西王博乂，高祖兄子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Longxi Boyi was a son of Gaozu's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Longxi Boyi was a son of Gaozu's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 高祖長兄曰澄，次曰湛，次曰洪，並早卒。

translations.literal: Gaozu's eldest brother was named Cheng; next came Zhan; next Hong—all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's eldest brother was named Cheng; next came Zhan; then Hong. All died young.

sentences.zh: 武德初，追封澄為梁王，湛為蜀王，洪為鄭王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, Cheng was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Liang, Zhan as Prince of Shu, and Hong as Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude, Cheng was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Liang, Zhan as Prince of Shu, and Hong as Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 澄、洪並無後，博乂即湛第二子也。

translations.literal: Cheng and Hong both left no heirs; Boyi was the second son of Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Hong both left no heirs. Boyi was the second son of Zhan.

sentences.zh: 武德元年受封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he received his enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he received his enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，歷宗正卿、禮部尚書，加特進。

translations.literal: During Gaozu's reign he served successively as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan and Minister of Rites, and was granted the honorary rank Tejin.
translations.idiomatic: During Gaozu's reign he served successively as chamberlain for the imperial clan and minister of rites, and was granted the honorary rank tejin.

sentences.zh: 博乂有妓妾數百人，皆衣羅綺，食必粱肉，朝夕纟玄歌自娛，驕侈無比。

translations.literal: Boyi kept several hundred singing-girl concubines; all wore silk gauze and brocade, ate nothing but fine grain and meat, amused themselves morning and evening with string music and song, and were extravagantly arrogant beyond compare.
translations.idiomatic: Boyi kept several hundred singing-girl concubines. All wore silk gauze and brocade, ate nothing but fine grain and meat, and amused themselves morning and evening with string music and song. His extravagance and arrogance were beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 與其弟渤海王奉慈俱為高祖所鄙，帝謂曰：「我怨仇有善，猶擢以不次，況於親戚而不委任？

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Prince of Bohai Fengci were both despised by Gaozu; the emperor said to them: "If even my enemies show merit, I still promote them out of turn—how much more should I not entrust affairs to kinsmen?
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Prince of Bohai Fengci were both despised by Gaozu. The emperor said to them, "If even my enemies show merit, I still promote them out of turn. How much more should I not entrust affairs to kinsmen?

sentences.zh: 聞汝等唯暱近小人，好為不軌，先王墳典，不聞習學。

translations.literal: I hear that you only fraternize with petty men and delight in unseemly conduct; of the canonical texts left by the former kings, I hear no word that you study them.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that you only fraternize with petty men and delight in unseemly conduct. Of the canonical texts left by the former kings, I hear no word that you study them.

sentences.zh: 今賜絹二百匹，可各買經史習讀，務為善事。」

translations.literal: Now I grant you two hundred bolts of silk apiece; you may each buy classics and histories and study them, and devote yourselves to good conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Now I grant you two hundred bolts of silk apiece. You may each buy classics and histories and study them, and devote yourselves to good conduct.

sentences.zh: 咸亨二年薨，贈開府儀同三司、荊州都督，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianheng he died; he was posthumously granted the title of Honorary Three Excellencies with privilege to maintain an office equal to a commandery governor's, and Area Commander of Jingzhou; his posthumous designation was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianheng he died. He was posthumously granted the title of honorary three excellencies with privilege to maintain an office equal to a commandery governor's, and area commander of Jingzhou. His posthumous name was Gong ["Respectful"].

sentences.zh: 奉慈，武德初，封渤海王。

translations.literal: Fengci—at the beginning of Wude was enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Fengci was enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai at the beginning of Wude.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，累遷原州都督，薨，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: During the Xianqing era he was successively promoted to Area Commander of Yuanzhou; he died; his posthumous designation was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianqing era he was successively promoted to area commander of Yuanzhou. He died, and his posthumous name was Jing ["Reverent"].

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：無私於物，物亦公焉。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When one is impartial toward things, things in turn respond with impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: When one is impartial toward things, things in turn respond with impartiality.

sentences.zh: 高祖才定中原，先封疏屬，致廬江為叛，神通爭功，封德彝論之於前，房玄齡譏之於後。

translations.literal: As soon as Gaozu had pacified the Central Plains he first enfeoffed distant kinsmen; this led Lujiang to rebel, and Shentong to wrangle over merit—Feng Deyi argued against it beforehand, and Fang Xuanling mocked it afterward.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Gaozu had pacified the Central Plains, he first enfeoffed distant kinsmen. This led Lujiang to rebel and Shentong to wrangle over merit. Feng Deyi argued against it beforehand, and Fang Xuanling mocked it afterward.

sentences.zh: 若河間機謀深沉，識度弘遠，縱虛舟而降蕭銑，飲妖血而平公祏，入朝定君臣之分，賣第為子孫之謀，善始令終，論功行賞，即無私矣。

translations.literal: Consider how Prince of Hejian's stratagems ran deep and his vision was broad: he released empty boats to induce Xiao Xian's surrender, drank demon blood to pacify Li Gongzuo, entered court to fix the distinction between minister and sovereign, sold his mansion for his descendants' sake, keeping a fine beginning and a fine end, assigning merit and granting rewards—in that lay true impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Prince of Hejian: his stratagems ran deep and his vision was broad. He released empty boats to induce Xiao Xian's surrender, drank demon blood to pacify Li Gongzuo, entered court to fix the distinction between minister and sovereign, and sold his mansion for his descendants' sake. Keeping a fine beginning and a fine end, assigning merit and granting rewards—in that lay true impartiality.

sentences.zh: 或問曰：「水變為血，信妖矣；

translations.literal: Someone asked: "When water turns to blood, it is truly an omen of ill;
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "When water turns to blood, that is surely an evil omen;

sentences.zh: 竟成功而無咎者，何也？」

translations.literal: yet in the end he succeeded without calamity—why?
translations.idiomatic: yet he succeeded in the end without suffering harm—how can that be?

sentences.zh: 答曰：河間節貫神明，志匡宗社，故妖不勝德明矣。

translations.literal: The answer was: Prince of Hejian's integrity penetrated the divine; his will was to set right the altars of state—therefore the omen could not overcome virtue, and this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: The reply was: Prince of Hejian's integrity reached to the gods, and his purpose was to restore the altars of state—so the omen could not prevail over virtue. That is plain enough.

sentences.zh: 道宗軍謀武勇，好學下賢，於群從之中，稱一時之傑。

translations.literal: Daozong was skilled in military strategy and martial valor, loved learning and honored the worthy, and among the collateral kin was called a hero of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong combined military counsel with martial courage, loved learning and honored men of talent, and among the collateral princes stood as the outstanding man of his generation.

sentences.zh: 無忌、遂良銜不協之素，致千載之冤。

translations.literal: Wuji and Suiliang long harbored old discord and brought about a wrong that would last a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and Suiliang had long nursed their mutual dislike and thereby inflicted a wrong that would echo for ages.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，無忌、遂良忠而獲罪，人皆哀之。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era Wuji and Suiliang, though loyal, were punished with crime, and all men pitied them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era Wuji and Suiliang were punished despite their loyalty, and everyone pitied them.

sentences.zh: 殊不知誣陷劉洎、吳王恪於前，枉害道宗於後，天網不漏，不得其死也宜哉！

translations.literal: They did not know that before this they had falsely implicated Liu Ji and Prince of Wu Ke, and afterward wrongfully harmed Daozong—the net of Heaven misses nothing; that they did not die a natural death was only fitting!
translations.idiomatic: They failed to see that they had earlier framed Liu Ji and Prince of Wu Ke, and later wronged Daozong unjustly—the net of Heaven misses nothing; that they did not die in their beds was only what they deserved!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：疏屬盡封，啟亂害公。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Distant kin all enfeoffed—this stirred disorder and harmed the public good.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Enfeoffing every distant clansman opened the way to disorder and harmed the public good.

sentences.zh: 河間孝恭，獨稱軍功。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Xiaogong alone was famed for military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince of Hejian Xiaogong won true renown on the battlefield.
